decisions.summary: one make detector shared by the log and the guards, the gate's crate-scoped form read as rust-<cmd>
decisions.why: FR-001's classing by target; fixes a found defect (R1) in the task touching it.

decisions.summary: one bucket_of table shared by writer and readers, readers book by the make field, every line carries task
decisions.why: FR-001's one table the readers share; re-booking a past log serves the GM's retrospective.

decisions.summary: bg on launch, BgEnd from the task-notification prompt, inflight on Stop; subagent ends from the subagent transcript
decisions.why: FR-002 and the approved 'logs that end from its completion notice'; the transcript read is where the plan states no hook carries a subagent run's end (R2).

decisions.summary: build, test, cover-run, lint and format phase lines per crate, wall-clock spans
decisions.why: FR-003 as written.

decisions.summary: cover-build phase line per family (naming its crates), not per crate
decisions.why: Physically impossible per crate: one coverage build compiles the family's crates at once, so no per-crate seconds exist to log. The line names every crate it served. The GM's own words ('append their phase seconds') carry no per-crate requirement, and the compile-vs-test split ('how much time ... recompiling') is kept whole.

decisions.summary: land writes cheap, gate, cohort, claims, push phases and an end line with exit code
decisions.why: FR-003 (make land's phases) and FR-005's refused-landing rework count.

decisions.summary: Agent PreToolUse records task; SubagentStop records deduplicated tok, ctx, task; reader keeps last per aid
decisions.why: FR-004 and the approved 'records it at each agent's stop'.

decisions.summary: where-time and feature-report read the same columns module; critical path apart from agent-minutes; rework counted; UNTIL=
decisions.why: FR-005 clause by clause.

decisions.summary: a builder is any agent whose agent_type names no .claude/agents file - every defined agent exempt, where the spec exempts a defined REVIEW agent
decisions.why: The spec's own exclusion, made mechanical. As the plan states (R3, not in the bundle), the rule caught every builder that passed the cap in the window. It would only reach too little if some defined agent that is not a reviewer were dispatched with a task's brief. If such an agent exists in .claude/agents, it must be capped too.

decisions.summary: a general-purpose agent dispatched with no task is capped too
decisions.why: It narrows nothing. The test is structural, so a builder cannot escape the cap through how its brief is worded, which is the real-enforcement reading. As the plan states, every general-purpose dispatch is a brief.

decisions.summary: context_cap_hooks refuses a builder's every call past CONTEXT_CAP_TOKENS (GUESS 300k) but the handoff Write; CONTEXT_OK or a recorded make context-ok permit escapes
decisions.why: FR-006 and FR-012. The knob is the spec's GUESS. The handoff Write is tested through the whole guard chain.

decisions.summary: SendMessage to a builder past the cap refused
decisions.why: FR-006 as written.

decisions.summary: SendMessage to a builder whose task has landed: the task is taken ONLY from the meta description's T<n>
decisions.why: FR-006 says a SendMessage resuming a builder whose task has landed is refused. D8 itself says a builder with an unnamed brief exists and must not slip through. Yet D10 finds the task only from a T<n> in the description, so for that builder the landed-task refusal never fires, and its resume leaves no record. Working out the task is not impossible: D2 already has a fallback chain (the task the agent's lines carry, else the clone's task-starts entry at its dispatch). Fix: D10 uses D2's chain, and a builder with any landing of its task after its dispatch is refused, with a red case for a builder whose description names no T<n>.

decisions.summary: every session's and agent's make static runs count toward the task, the main session's too
decisions.why: FR-007 counts runs in one task and names no agent.

decisions.summary: the count window starts at the later of the task's last task-starts entry and its last landing
decisions.why: FR-007 has one reset: 'since its last landing'. Lines are already filtered by task, so a start bound adds nothing except a second reset, and the plan gives no reason for it. Whether an open task can gain a second task-starts entry is unmeasured. If it can, running task-start again zeroes the count with no recorded escape, which turns the refusal into an instruction. Fix: count the task's static lines since its last landing only (or since its FIRST start where it has never landed), with a red case where a second task-start does not reset the count.

decisions.summary: a make or cargo run backgrounded with & and then waited on in the same call passes
decisions.why: The approved fix targets a run whose end no notice reports ('no completion notice came, and it sat idle'). A call that waits on its job does not return before the run ends, so the harness tracks it. Refusing it would refuse a tracked run and serve none of the rule's purpose.

decisions.summary: the pass test is 'no wait later in the command': no command position for wait, and nothing ties the wait to the make job
decisions.why: D12a's reason holds only for a wait that covers the make job, but the plan's test is any later 'wait'. Under it, `make static & echo wait` and `make static & sleep 5 & wait $!` (which waits only for the sleep) both pass, return with the run detached, and leave no record: exactly T225's untracked run. The plan already asks command position for nohup, setsid and disown, and asks none for wait. Fix: pass only a wait at a command position that covers the make or cargo job (a bare wait, or wait $!/%N naming that job with no & between), with red cases for the two forms above.

decisions.summary: main session only (no agent_id), on both permitted no-poll paths including the POLL_OK-escaped loop, longest sleep over POLL_CHECK_S (GUESS 60 s) refused; SLOW_POLL_OK escapes
decisions.why: FR-008 as written. POLL_OK does not bypass it.

decisions.summary: knobs recorded as GUESS constants and a docs/guards.md knob table; make tunables not extended to the tooling crates
decisions.why: The GM's request names no knob register and no make tunables, and no cited FR does either, so leaving tunables as it is narrows nothing asked. The spec's Assumptions text was not in the bundle, so this rests on the plan's statement that the spec names tunables only as where retuning happens.

decisions.summary: a deferral must carry a reason, 'a task id T<n>' and 'lands before T<n>' - checked as a form, not as a FILED task
decisions.why: FR-009 asks for 'its filed task id'. The plan checks for a string T<n>, so a made-up id that is in no tasks.md passes make decide with no record: a form check where the request asked for real enforcement. Checking it is cheap (the feature's tasks.md and tasks-done.md). Fix: the deferral's T<n>, and its lands-before T<n>, must name tasks filed in the feature, with a red case for an unfiled id.

decisions.summary: a class-of-defect fix must carry an observed-date-and-method line
decisions.why: FR-009's second clause as written.

decisions.summary: make land splits T= on commas and whitespace
decisions.why: FR-011, the approved 'Accept commas in T='.

decisions.summary: task-add: if quick is still red after withdrawing the line, the line is restored and the run only reports - no comparison of failures
decisions.why: FR-011 refuses 'on any failure the new line introduces'. When make quick is already red for another reason, a line that adds a failure of its own is restored and passes with no record (T19's third case pins this). It is not impossible to catch: compare the failures with the line to those without it. Fix: refuse and withdraw whenever the with-line run has a failure the without-line run lacks, and keep the line only when the failures are the same; add a red case with a pre-existing failure plus the line's own.

decisions.summary: suites split into numbered shards, the runner stamps the suite when every shard is green, SHARD_BAR_S GUESS about 20 s measured, never a gate
decisions.why: FR-010 and SC-004.

decisions.summary: One make detector shared by the event log and every guard; command positions also take (, flock, nice, time, timeout N; l7r-gate.sh rust <cmd> read as rust-<cmd>.
decisions.why: FR-001 classes each make run by target; one detector is how that holds. Unchanged since the last reading.

decisions.summary: One bucket_of table shared by writer and readers, past logs re-booked by their make field; every line carries task (T= of the command, else the subagent meta description's T<n>, else the clone's last task-starts entry).
decisions.why: FR-001's 'by one table the readers share'; the task field serves the GM's per-task breakdown. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Background run end from the task-notification prompt (BgEnd), inflight on Stop/SubagentStop, subagent ends from their transcript's queued_command row, an unended run open to the window's end.
decisions.why: FR-002 as written, which is the approved 'logs that end from its completion notice'. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Phase lines carry wall-clock spans; coverage builds are timed per family (naming the family's crates), not per crate.
decisions.why: FR-003 says per crate, but one coverage build serves a whole family at once and the runs go side by side (R6), so a per-crate cover-build time cannot be measured. That is physical impossibility. The line still names every crate in the family. Unchanged since the last reading, so the ruling stands.

decisions.summary: land writes cheap/gate/cohort/claims/push Phase lines and an end line with its exit code and tasks (T= split as D16), read by D10 and D11 for foreground and background landings alike.
decisions.why: FR-003's landing phases and FR-005's rework count. The new tasks field is how D10 and D11 recognize a landing, so it only enforces FR-006 and FR-007.

decisions.summary: Agent dispatch task from its description; SubagentStop records tok (deduped by message.id), ctx and task; the reader keeps the last per aid.
decisions.why: FR-004 as written. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: where-time gains the tests/compile/gate/land/review/background/model columns and UNTIL=; critical path apart from agent-minutes; rework = refused landings plus plan re-rounds; feature-report reads the same columns module.
decisions.why: FR-005 clause by clause; it is the GM's request for the overall breakdown. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: A builder is a payload with agent_id whose agent_type names no .claude/agents/<type>.md; a general-purpose agent with no task is capped too.
decisions.why: This is a mechanical test of the spec's definition ('dispatched with a task's brief, not a defined review agent'). Requiring a T<n> would let a builder with an unnamed brief through the cap, which would not be real enforcement. Anything it over-catches has the recorded make context-ok escape. Unchanged since the last reading, so it carries forward. Note: 'among defined agents, one call' is a count with no date or method; it is unchanged text and does not block.

decisions.summary: context_cap_hooks: past CONTEXT_CAP_TOKENS (GUESS 300k), a builder's every tool call is refused except the Write of its handoff file, naming the path and next step; escapes CONTEXT_OK and a recorded make context-ok permit; the handoff case runs through the whole guard chain.
decisions.why: FR-006's cap and handoff exit, with the escape and message FR-012 requires. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Resume refused for a builder past the cap or whose task SUCCESSFULLY landed (end code 0 naming it, or ticked or archived) after dispatch. The task is found by meta T<n>, else its FIRST line's task, else the task-starts entry in force at dispatch.
decisions.why: FR-006 as written. The revision closes what the last round raised: no description-only lookup, the first line rather than the latest, the entry in force at dispatch, a background landing found through its end line's tasks, a refused landing not counted. T13 carries a red case for each of these.

decisions.summary: When no task can be found anywhere (no T<n>, no line carrying one, no task-starts entry before dispatch), the resume passes and 'context-cap: resume, no task' is written to the guard log.
decisions.why: Physically impossible: with no task there is nothing to test for having landed. It is only reachable when the feature had no task-start before the dispatch, because D2 stamps every later line with the active task. The pass leaves a record. LEGITIMATE only for the landed half. A builder past the cap with no task is still refused, because the bullet does not reach the cap. The plan should say so, and T13 should carry a case for it (see the D15 entry's list).

decisions.summary: static_runs_hooks counts a task's make static PreToolUse lines (every session and agent) since its last SUCCESSFUL landing, else since its FIRST task-start; a later task-start resets nothing; the third is refused naming the delta's crate-scoped checks; STATIC_OK escapes; knob GUESS 2.
decisions.why: FR-007 literally: 'a third make static in one task since its last landing'. It counts by task, so the main session's runs count too. The revision removes the last round's unrecorded resets (a second task-start, a refused landing), and T14 carries a red case for each.

decisions.summary: A make or cargo job followed by & is refused unless a wait that COVERS it follows: at a command position, in the same list and shell, unconditional, not backgrounded, and bare, wait $! with no & between, or wait %N. nohup/setsid/disown at a command position are refused. A saved-pid wait is refused. DETACH_OK escapes.
decisions.why: FR-008 lists & with no exception. But the approved fix was 'a guard refusing that pattern', meaning T225's detached run whose end the session never learned of. A covering wait keeps the Bash call open until the run ends, so the harness tracks it. The exception is implied by the request's own words, and refusing it would serve no part of the request's purpose. The revision makes 'covers' real: words, other shells, conditional waits, a backgrounded wait and a stale $! are all refused, each with a T15 red case. Refusing the saved-pid form is stricter than FR-008 and is within it. Notes, not blocking: wait %N has no case either way in T15; setsid and disown have no firing case (only nohup does); and whether D1 sees '{ ...; } &', 'VAR=x make ... &' or 'env ... make &' cannot be judged from this bundle, so T02 or T15 should pin those forms.

decisions.summary: On both permitted no-poll paths, a main-session (no agent_id) loop whose longest sleep exceeds POLL_CHECK_S (GUESS 60 s) is refused naming the 60 s form; SLOW_POLL_OK escapes.
decisions.why: FR-008's second clause. It turns the approved 'shorter poll loop on my side' into a refusal, as 'real enforcement' asks. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Knobs carry GUESS at their point of change and a knob table in docs/guards.md; make tunables is not extended to the tooling crates.
decisions.why: The GM's request never mentions make tunables. Its mention is a spec Assumption about where retuning happens, and the knob table (knob, value, label, the data that retunes it) serves the same purpose. Unchanged since the last reading, so the ruling stands.

decisions.summary: deferral_unformed: a non-none Found-and-left item must carry a reason, a task id and 'lands before T<n>', both ids FILED in the feature (a box of tasks.md OR an entry of tasks-done.md); a class fix needs an 'observed <date>, method:' line; DEFER_FORM_OK escapes.
decisions.why: FR-009 asks for 'its filed task id and its order ("lands before ...")', so that a deferred defect actually gets fixed, and in a known order (the approved 'briefs that default to fixing in the task'). Accepting an entry of tasks-done.md, which T17's second variant passes on purpose, guts both. (a) An order 'lands before T124' where T124 has already landed cannot be kept, so it orders nothing. (b) A deferral to a task that is already done will never be fixed by that task. Any feature has dozens of done ids, so a done id passes the check as easily as the made-up id the last round flagged: the hole has moved, not closed. That is a word-level reading of 'filed' that is fatal to the rule's purpose. Required, all in one revision: (1) at make decide, when the item is judged, both ids must name an OPEN task (an unticked box in the feature's tasks.md), and a section already decided is not refused later because an id it named has since landed; (2) the order's id differs from the deferral's own task id ('T123 lands before T123' is refused); (3) T17 drops the passing tasks-done variant and adds refused cases for a done deferral id, a done order id and a self-order, plus the case T17's own heading names and its list lacks: a reason and a filed task id with no 'lands before' at all, refused. Also, from D10-no-task: say that a builder past the cap with no task is still refused, and add that case to T13.

decisions.summary: land splits T= on commas and whitespace. task-add runs quick's check lines (from make -n quick) each to its own end, with and without the line, compares the findings as a multiset with line and column numbers masked, refuses and withdraws on any new finding, and restores the line only when the findings are identical; QUICK_OK escapes.
decisions.why: FR-011 as written. 'On any failure the new line introduces, withdraws the line and refuses' now holds even when an earlier check is already red or a finding in the same file is shifted, and T19 carries a red case for each. Restoring the line when the findings are the same is FR-011's own boundary (the line introduced no failure), not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: Hook suites may be sharded as test-<name>.<k>.sh, stamped green when every shard is; entry-gate split by its two cases, the other two by case groups to about 20 s or less (SHARD_BAR_S GUESS, measured, never a gate).
decisions.why: FR-010 and SC-004. The approved improvement 5 is a split, not a refusal, so FR-012 does not reach it. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Constitution check: event_log_hooks fields move to fields.rs past the file cap; XIII baseline in a detached worktree; the two defects found while measuring (the disagreeing make detectors, booking by the frozen cat) are fixed in T02 and T08.
decisions.why: Process the constitution requires; the XIV fixes are defects (wrong answers) inside FR-001 and FR-005's own scope.

decisions.summary: T12 first captures a real subagent PreToolUse payload under L7R_GUARD_DUMP, removed before landing, and pins it as the fixture.
decisions.why: It measures the schema the cap depends on (R2's 'not yet observed') and adds no behavior that survives the landing.

decisions.summary: The close measures SC-001, SC-002 and SC-005 on the first full day after landing, checks the knob table, and writes the feature report.
decisions.why: The spec's success criteria, measured as the request asks ('I'd like to see some actual numbers').

decisions.why: This is T05's row form applied to this source.

decisions.why: A stop is not a refusal, and a landing stopped before its push did not land. Reading it as open answers D7, D10 and D11 correctly. The running step's split is lost, but FR-002 still books the run's span.

decisions.summary: A landing stopped in the push's tail (after-push) already has its end written, landed true
decisions.why: This closes the previous round's NOT LEGITIMATE finding. The end at the push now carries landed true before the tail starts, so D10 and D11 read the task as landed, and red-first cases cover a tail that raises after the push.

decisions.summary: One window stays open. A stop while sync-with-main.sh done runs, after the remote took the push but before the script reports it, writes no end. The section points to the push's tick commit on main as the record
decisions.why: Last round's exception rested on implementation awkwardness ('no signal handler's work'). This one rests on knowledge: until the push command reports, the landing process does not hold the fact that the remote took the push, so no writer in the landing can record landed true in that interval. A pre-push guess would write a false landed whenever the push then fails. The rule is impossible here, not merely awkward, and the section has already shrunk the gap to that interval. The tick commit on main is not what makes this legitimate: D10 and D11 as cited read the end line, not main. The real outcome in the window is that the landing reads as open, never as refused. D7's rework count therefore stays right, D10 misses a resume of that task's builder, and D11 keeps that task's static count unreset. That is one rare interleaving (a manual stop during the push itself), with the outcome confined to that one task. This is the one case the previous round's requirement ('once a landing's push has gone out, a later stop must not leave it reading as unlanded') cannot reach. The ruling covers only the interval before the script reports the push went out. The block also says 'before the script exits'. If sync-with-main.sh reports success and then goes on working before it exits, that stretch is not unknowable: end must be written when the report comes, and an end held until the exit would be outside this ruling.

decisions.summary: A make static still in flight (no PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure line yet), e.g. a foreground run in another session of the same task, is not yet counted.
decisions.why: Ruled on purpose. The request's improvement 2 targets make static as the edit loop: each iteration of a loop waits for the previous run's result, so every run that feeds a loop has its result line and is counted; the in-flight window only admits a run concurrent with another in the same task, and that run is counted the moment it finishes, so the next call is refused. The edit-loop pattern cannot live in the gap; the purpose survives. Not ruled on an impossibility claim (the bundle does not measure whether the guard log could tell a refused call from an in-flight one).

decisions.summary: The event log writer adds `makes` (every target of a multi-target call) and the count reads `make` or `makes`, so `make rust-test CRATE=x && make static` is counted.

decisions.why: FR-007 refuses a third `make static`; a call refused before it ran is not a run on the plain reading. D11 as now quoted in spec-cited.md carries this definition (a run is a call that RAN, T14 2026-11-20), and it matches the request's improvement 2 rather than narrowing it.

decisions.summary: A make static still in flight (no PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure line yet), e.g. a foreground run in another session of the same task, is not yet counted.
decisions.why: Unchanged from the earlier ruling, on purpose: improvement 2 targets make static as the edit loop, and each iteration of a loop waits for the previous run's result, so every run feeding a loop has its result line and is counted; the gap admits only a run concurrent with another in the same task, counted the moment it finishes. The edit-loop pattern cannot live in the gap, so the request's purpose survives.

decisions.summary: The event log writer adds `makes` (every target of a multi-target call) and the count reads `make` or `makes`, so `make rust-test CRATE=x && make static` is counted.
decisions.why: Enforcement of FR-007 (and now in D11's text): without it a compound call escapes the count while the trigger fires on it. Delete FR-007 and the field has nothing to do.

decisions.summary: Count keyed on (feature, task) via filed_at's chain, reading only that feature's log; main session and builders share one count.
decisions.why: FR-007 counts per task; D11: every session and agent's run counts.

decisions.summary: Since the task's last landing with landed true naming it in `tasks` (any exit code), else its FIRST task-starts entry (second stamp compared as .000Z), else every line.
decisions.why: FR-007 'since its last landing'; D11/D10's definition (landed true resets, a refused landing does not; a later task-start resets nothing). Reading `tasks` makes a batch landing reset each of its tasks.

decisions.summary: A call whose line carries no task passes, logged passed/no-task.
decisions.why: FR-007 is scoped 'in one task'; D2 files a task wherever one is known (falling back to the clone's last task-start), so a call with no task has nothing to count against. The block's citation of 'D10's precedent' is still not supported by D10 as quoted; the decision stands on FR-007 and D2.

decisions.summary: Refusal names, per crate of the delta, `make rust-test CRATE=<c>` and the gate script's lint/format/cover --crate; `make quick` when no crate changed; then make static once before land; STATIC_OK escape with a reason; each named command pinned as passing the Bash-reading guards.
decisions.why: FR-007 'naming the crate-scoped checks for the crates the task's delta changes'; FR-012 'a message naming the compliant command' and a recorded escape. The dispatch states STATIC_OK's reason goes through the shared escape reader's two-word floor (FR-012); the block's 'a bare token refused' is consistent with it, and no decision here lowers that floor.

decisions.summary: Knob STATIC_RUNS_A_TASK, GUESS, 2; documented in docs/guards.md's knob table.
decisions.why: D11 and D14 as written.

decisions.summary: Unit and suite cases for each count/reset/exclusion and escape; condition switched off turns 8 of 11 count tests and 9 of 17 suite checks red.
decisions.why: FR-012 red-first; enforcement of FR-007 (one-shot labeled measurements).

decisions.summary: Tagged [perf], placed in lane A after T18 and T28.
decisions.why: FR-013 and the GM's 2026-11-20 order: these improvements first.

decisions.summary: docs/guards.md row and knob row, rust/guard/CLAUDE.md mention, D11 and data-model.md restated - T14's own, written before its tick.
decisions.why: D14 and the documentation duty, held as T14's own work and not deferred. D11's restatement is visible in spec-cited.md; the other files' being written is the block's and dispatch's word (the bundle excludes the repository).

decisions.summary: Guard crate tests of six other guards fail under an exported L7R_FEATURE_DIRECTORY; filed as T32, landing before T22.
decisions.why: A defect (a check failing good work in a page session) not left: filed as a named task in this feature before T22 (SC-005's measurement), with why it is not fixed here (outside T14's files) and how every instance was found, as FR-009 asks.

decisions.summary: guard_file_hooks refuses sed -i on a guard file but not a Python heredoc writing it; filed as T33, landing before T22.
decisions.why: A defect (a guard passing what it exists to stop), filed as a named task in this feature before T22, outside T14's files; not carried past the feature.

decisions.summary: No make target formats one file; filed as T34, landing before T22.
decisions.why: A tooling gap rather than a defect; filing it narrows nothing of the request.

decisions.summary: D11 restated: a run counted is a make static call that RAN (its PreToolUse line has a PostToolUse or PostToolUseFailure line); a call another guard refused is not counted; the `makes` field (every target of a compound call) is read beside `make`.
decisions.why: FR-007 refuses 'a third make static'; a call another guard refused ran no make static, so not counting it is the plain reading, and counting it would spend the task's budget on nothing and could bar the approved 'make static once at the end'. Reading `makes` widens the count to compound calls D11's trigger already fires on - enforcement of FR-007, not new scope.

decisions.summary: The stated cost of counting only runs that ran: a FOREGROUND make static still in flight in another session of the same task is not yet counted.
decisions.why: The edit loop FR-007 exists to stop (improvement 2: 'T152 ran it 24 times') is sequential, and every completed or failed run is counted; a run_in_background launch gets its PostToolUse at once (D3, D10), so the normal long form is counted at launch. The residue is at most one extra run in a race between two agents running make static on the same task at once, which does not gut the purpose; the alternative (bare PreToolUse lines) charges refused attempts as runs, refusing correct work. Separate from D11-ran, which is within.

decisions.summary: Since: the last landing whose end line reads landed true and whose `tasks` names the task, strictly after; else the FIRST task-starts entry from that second on (to-the-second stamp read as .000Z); else every line.
decisions.why: Restates D10/D11 as already CLEAR (a second task-start resets nothing, a refused landing resets nothing); the timestamp alignment is mechanism.

decisions.summary: A call whose line carries no task at all passes, written to the guard log as passed/no-task.
decisions.why: FR-007 counts 'a third make static in one task'; D2's chain ends at the clone's task-starts entry for the feature, so a line with no task means no task exists to count in - implied by the requirement's own words. The pass is recorded (D10's precedent), so it leaves a trace.

decisions.summary: The refusal names, per crate the delta changes (merge-base diff plus untracked files, mapped to the nearest [package] Cargo.toml), make rust-test CRATE=<c> and l7r-gate rust lint/format --check/cover --crate <c>; with no crate in the delta, make quick; then make static once before make land; STATIC_OK with a reason.
decisions.why: FR-007 names the crate-scoped checks for the crates the delta changes; adding untracked files to the delta and naming make quick when no crate changed only completes the message for the case FR-007 leaves empty.

decisions.summary: The docs/guards.md row, the STATIC_RUNS_A_TASK knob-table row (D14), the rust/guard/CLAUDE.md mention and D11's restatement (with data-model.md's field list) are T14's own, now written by the session before its tick.
decisions.why: Not a deferral; T14's own documentation, done before the tick.

decisions.summary: Found and left: 17-20 tests of six other guards fail with L7R_FEATURE_DIRECTORY exported; why not here (six other guards' tests, outside T14's files), how every instance was found (the crate's whole test run under the export), filed as T32, lands before T22.

decisions.summary: As built: the pace is the longest sleep at a command position inside a loop (head counted), units s/m/h/d read and summed, a -c string read; in no_poll_hooks/pace.rs (split at the 1,000-line bar); checked first on the POLL_OK branch and before file_wait; a payload with agent_id passes the pace check untouched; SLOW_POLL_OK masked before POLL_OK is read.
decisions.why: FR-008 and D13: a main-session permitted wait loop slower than 60 s is refused naming the 60 s form; subagents are outside 'in the main session'. The file split is housekeeping.

decisions.summary: A loop sleep given a variable the command sets is read at the largest value set; any length still unreadable (variable set nowhere, arithmetic, substitution, infinity) is refused as endless naming the literal sleep 60 form, SLOW_POLL_OK escaping; red first, 24 judgments.
decisions.why: The previous NOT LEGITIMATE narrowing (an unread pace passing) is gone: the variable form is now enforced, as D12 enforces an unreadable wait $P. Refusing what cannot be read is enforcement of FR-008's 60 s rule in the main session only, with the FR-012 escape and named compliant form - not new scope.

decisions.summary: Found and fixed: a loop whose sleep takes a variable never reached the loop branch (SLEEP_RE and sleep_in_loop ask for a digit), so `until curl -s x; do sleep $N; done` passed even the existing busy-wait refusal, subagents included; the branch is now entered where the pace reader finds a sleep in a loop.
decisions.why: A pre-existing defect of an existing guard (it passed a form it exists to refuse), found in the task and fixed in it per fix-as-we-go; it adds no new refusal reach, it closes a hole in one already approved.

decisions.summary: Before any fix: shared::wait's grammar did not read proof_of_life's clause, so the guard refused its own file-wait rewrite when re-run; fixed in T16, red first.
decisions.why: A pre-existing defect found in the task and fixed in it (fix as we go).

decisions.summary: POLL_CHECK_S goes into D14's knob table with T22, which is the close.
decisions.why: Documentation placement already ordered to an open, named task; not a defect.

blocks: ### T16 (FR-008: the main session's waits checked every 420 to 600 s, observed 2026-11-19, method: the wait commands of the main session's transcript - the spec's User Story 4, research R5)

decisions.summary: slow_poll (split into no_poll_hooks/pace.rs under constitution X's 1,000-line bar) is called first in the POLL_OK-escaped branch and before file_wait; a payload with agent_id passes untouched by the pace check; -c strings and backgrounded calls are judged too
decisions.why: This is D13 as written: both permitted paths, before either returns, and the main session only (no agent_id). A -c string that a shell runs is the same loop spelled another way, so reading it enforces FR-008 and adds no reach. Splitting the file is housekeeping, not a decision about scope.

decisions.summary: the pace is the longest sleep at a command position inside a loop, with the head counted, s/m/h/d units read and several numbers summed as GNU sleep reads them; a quoted string, a sleep with no loop, a sleep after done and a redirection after a sleep are not a pace
decisions.why: FR-008 refuses a 'wait loop' that checks less often than 60 s. Reading the loop's real interval the way the shell would is that rule. A sleep outside a loop and a quoted string are not a checking loop, so passing them follows FR-008's wording.

decisions.summary: replaces the earlier pass of sleep $N: a variable the command sets (N=480, export, quoted, an env prefix, several assignments) is read at the largest value it is given, and a length still unreadable ($N set nowhere, arithmetic, a substitution, infinity) is refused as endless, naming the literal sleep 60 form, with SLOW_POLL_OK as the escape
decisions.why: This no longer narrows. Every main-session wait loop now gets judged, which is FR-008's rule with no carve-out. Refusing a length the guard cannot read is enforcement of the requested rule, not new behavior. The guard cannot show that such a loop checks within 60 s. The refusal names the compliant form and offers FR-012's recorded escape. The spec already does the same for D12's unreadable 'wait $P'. Taking the largest value assigned is a conservative reading of the same rule. The GM asked for 'real enforcement and not just instructions', and this closes the gap my earlier ruling left open. The plan-blocks review overruled that ruling (LEGITIMATE), and this block follows the review.

decisions.summary: a pre-existing defect is fixed: SLEEP_RE and sleep_in_loop required a digit, so a loop whose sleep takes a variable (until curl -s x; do sleep $N; done) never reached the loop branch and passed even the busy-wait refusal, a subagent's included. The branch is now entered wherever the pace reader finds a sleep in a loop
decisions.why: Under constitution XIV this is a defect: a check that passes bad work. HEAD's guard was observed letting the loop through (rc 0, with a method recorded). It sits in the file and the reader T16 changes, and fixing defects as they are found is the standing rule. The fix does not create new behavior. It makes the existing busy-wait refusal reach a spelling that had slipped past it, and the frozen corpora show 0 of 1,134 verdicts moved. That is consistent with 'the existing no-poll cases unchanged'.

decisions.summary: the refusal names the same command with every sleep over the knob at sleep 60. SLOW_POLL_OK escapes and is recorded, and it is masked before POLL_OK is read, so it grants nothing POLL_OK grants. Thin reasons (empty, one word quoted or bare, one word after the colon) are refused and pinned
decisions.why: D13 names the compliant form and the SLOW_POLL_OK escape. FR-012 requires an escape with a reason of two words or more, recorded, and a message naming the compliant command. Pinning the refusal of one-word reasons enforces FR-012's exact wording. The masking makes the escape do only what it says.

decisions.summary: the guard's own rewrites and offers, fed back from the main session, are never refused for their pace
decisions.why: Those forms are at or under the knob, so FR-008 does not reach them. Testing that they pass enforces the compliant side of the rule.

decisions.summary: a defect that predates T16 is fixed: shared::wait's condition grammar did not read proof_of_life's clause, so the guard refused its own invited file-wait rerun as a busy-wait. One existing test's expectation is changed to ask that the fed-back wait get no answer
decisions.why: The guard was refusing correct work on one of D13's two permitted paths, the path T16 adds its check to. That is a defect under XIV and is fixed as the work goes. The changed test is where the defect was hidden ('rewritten()' read a refusal as no rewrite), so changing it does not depart from 'the existing no-poll cases unchanged'.

decisions.summary: POLL_CHECK_S = 60 s, labeled GUESS at its point of change
decisions.why: FR-008 and D13 name the knob as 60 s and GUESS, and D14 asks for the label at the point of change.

decisions.summary: POLL_CHECK_S's row in D14's knob table in docs/guards.md is left to T22, which writes that table and is the close
decisions.why: This is ordering, not a narrowing. The table is still delivered inside the feature, before it closes, by the task that writes it. It is not a deferred defect, so FR-009 does not reach it. That T22 writes the table rests on the block's word, which this bundle cannot confirm.

decisions.summary: T16 is tagged [perf] under FR-013
decisions.why: T16 is improvement 3 of the six the GM approved ('a shorter poll loop on my side', 18 min). The GM ruled on 2026-11-20 that those fixes come first because 'doing those first makes everything after them faster'. Under FR-013 it makes the builders' loop faster.

decisions.summary: Past the cap the handoff passes as a Write, Edit or Read of <git common dir>/l7r-handoffs/<task>-<agent id>.md (any file there ending <agent id>.md is the agent's); every other call refused naming it.
decisions.why: FR-006 lets through 'writing its handoff file'. Edit is a write; Read of that one file is what the Write tool needs before it can overwrite the file. Keying by agent id keeps each builder to its own file, and another agent's handoff is refused. Nothing outside the handoff is let through.

decisions.summary: The per-agent `make context-ok` permit is built with T13 (D10's resume) instead of T12; until then CONTEXT_OK in a Bash call is the recorded escape. Deferral formed: why, filed as T13, lands before T22.
decisions.why: The permit stays in the plan and in this feature. It moves to the task that builds the resume it serves, so this is a change of order inside the feature, not a cut from what was asked. Until T13 lands the cap is still enforced, with a recorded two-word escape through Bash (FR-012). The missing permit only makes the guard stricter, which matches the GM's 'real enforcement and not just instructions'.

decisions.summary: No transcript file, or no assistant row with nonzero usage in the tail (at most 16 MiB), passes; only assistant rows count, and a zero row is synthetic.
decisions.why: The cap is on a context the guard measures. Where there is nothing to measure the rule cannot be applied at all. Counting only assistant rows is the measured way to read the builder's own context (user rows carry the child's usage, observed 2026-11-20), so it is how the rule is met, not a way around it.

decisions.summary: An agent_id that is not a plain name (letters, digits, -, _) passes.
decisions.why: Such an id cannot safely be joined into the transcript path or the handoff name, so the guard cannot read the context or name the handoff file, which is the cap's one exit. Real agent ids are plain names (the captured payloads), so in practice this does not weaken the rule.

decisions.summary: A call outside any clone passes.
decisions.why: FR-006's one exit is a handoff file under <git common dir>/l7r-handoffs, and D8 decides who is a builder from the clone's .claude/agents. Outside a clone neither exists. A refusal there would leave no exit to write and no way to tell a builder from a defined agent, so the rule as written cannot be applied.

decisions.summary: CONTEXT_OK="<reason>" in a Bash command passes and is recorded; a bare one is refused. Red-first and check-deleted runs recorded.
decisions.why: This is FR-012's escape and its red-first proof.

decisions.summary: An item passes as `none`, `fixed here` (or fixed before its tick, or before T<own> lands) or `not a defect` / `no wrong outcome`; an item that names a filed or order id is judged as a deferral whatever else it says.
decisions.why: FR-009 refuses an item that DEFERS a defect. An item fixed in the task defers nothing, and one that is not a defect (constitution XIV) is not a deferred defect. Any item naming a task it is filed under is still judged as a deferral, so these phrases cannot be used to dodge the rule. The earlier D15 demanded the form of every non-none item, which went past FR-009, so this brings the plan back to the spec rather than narrowing it.

decisions.summary: A deferral owes `Not fixed here` with two words of reason, `filed as T<n>` (or `added to` / `folded into`), `lands before T<m>`, ids distinct, each filed (timeless, plan-delta) and open (decide).
decisions.why: These are FR-009's 'why the defect is not fixed in this task, its filed task id and its order'. Adding to or folding into an existing task is still a filed task id.

decisions.summary: A class fix is detected by `every` / `all the` before writer, reader, form, file, caller, instance, copy, site or guard, or `each of the`; it owes an observed/measured label with its method; checklist item 12 is judged too.
decisions.why: FR-009 defines a class by its examples: every writer, every form, every file of a kind. The detector catches all three and more. A bare `all` would refuse correct text such as 'all tests pass'.

decisions.summary: DEFER_FORM_OK is read from the environment and recorded by the tool itself (guard log rule defer-form-ok, and dev/bypass-log/), only on a run that passes or excuses a finding; plan-delta honors a decide-time escape and takes its own; a thin reason is refused on both verbs.
decisions.why: FR-012 asks for an escape whose reason is recorded, and this records it once. Changing the mechanism from $(LOGESCAPE) to the T28 form changes how the record is written, not what the requirement covers.

decisions.summary: plan-done.md sections are never judged (decide and plan-delta read plan.md only); the replay's 28 refusals are all archived.
decisions.why: FR-009 refuses at `make decide`. Archived sections are never decided again. No live plan.md section is refused (replay measured 2026-11-20).

decisions.summary: Two new task sections left as the unfilled template, whose Found-and-left placeholder states D15's form.
decisions.why: Placeholders decide nothing. The placeholder's wording is D15's 'template states the form'.

blocks: ### T17 (FR-009: two of the window's first-round plan-review blocks were deferrals with no order - the spec's User Story 5)

decisions.summary: A found-and-left item that says it is fixed in the task (fixed here, fixed in this task, before its tick, before T<own> lands) passes without a reason, filed id and order, unless it names an id it is filed as or lands before.
decisions.why: D15's visible sentence requires every non-none item to carry reason, id and order, so this narrows D15's text. But FR-009 refuses only an item that DEFERS a defect, and an item fixed in the task defers nothing; the GM approved 'briefs that default to fixing in the task', so requiring a filed task id of an item that is fixed would contradict the request. The guard that an item naming a filed/order id is judged as a deferral keeps the pass from being used to hide one.

decisions.summary: An item that says it is not a defect (not a defect, no wrong outcome, constitution XIV) passes.
decisions.why: Narrows D15's 'any non-none item' wording, but FR-009's own words reach only an item that 'defers a defect', and constitution XIV (the GM 2026-11-19) holds that a difference with no wrong outcome is not a defect and is not to be fixed. Demanding a filed fix task for a non-defect would apply a standard the GM struck. Same id-naming guard applies.

decisions.summary: A deferral owes 'Not fixed here' plus two words of reason, filed as T<n> (or added to / folded into), lands before T<m> (lists read whole), order id not equal to filed id, each id a box of tasks.md or tasks-done.md; make decide adds that each id is an unticked box now.
decisions.why: This is FR-009's three parts (why, filed id, order) made checkable; added to / folded into still name a filed task id; the open test at make decide makes the order real enforcement as the GM asked.

decisions.summary: A class fix is detected by every/all the before writer, reader, form, file, caller, instance, copy, site or guard, or 'each of the', and then owes an observed/measured line with its method.
decisions.why: FR-009's named forms (every writer, every form, every file of a kind) are all reached and the list is a superset of them; a mechanical trigger has to be a word test, and nothing FR-009 names falls outside it.

decisions.summary: The class test reads the found-and-left items and checklist item 12 (Before any fix).
decisions.why: FR-009 asks about the section's FIX; in the plan template the fix is declared in item 12 and the found-and-left answer, so reading those is reading the fix.

decisions.summary: make plan-delta runs the timeless half (form and ids filed in tasks.md or tasks-done.md) on a changed block; a section whose deferral's task has since landed is not refused.
decisions.why: FR-009 names make decide; running the same rule on a later edit only enforces it against a decided section being changed into an unformed one (the GM: 'real enforcement and not just instructions'). Not requiring the ids to be open after landing narrows nothing FR-009 asks, which is a check at decision time.

decisions.summary: A section decided under DEFER_FORM_OK passes make plan-delta after its block changes, the escape found in the guard log; the escape excuses only deferral findings.
decisions.why: It relaxes only the plan-delta check, which is enforcement beyond FR-009's make decide; at make decide, where FR-009 places the refusal, nothing is relaxed, and the escape was recorded with its reason as FR-012 requires.

decisions.summary: The tool records DEFER_FORM_OK itself (guard log rule defer-form-ok and dev/bypass-log/) instead of D15's $(LOGESCAPE) line, and only on a run that passes (decide once decided, plan-delta only where it excused a finding); a thin reason is refused.
decisions.why: FR-012 asks for an escape of two words or more that is recorded; it is recorded, once, whenever it is used. A run that is refused or excuses nothing did not use the escape. Mechanism choice; D15's text is restated to match (found-and-left).

decisions.summary: make plan-delta reads the guard log only for a changed block with a deferral finding, once a run, parsing only files naming the rule.
decisions.why: A cost choice that changes no outcome.

decisions.summary: plan-done.md is never read by make decide or plan-delta and the tick and landing call neither, so the 28 refused archived sections are not re-judged.
decisions.why: FR-009 is a refusal at make decide of a section being decided; archived sections were decided and ticked before the rule existed and no make decide runs on them. Nothing FR-009 asks is left out.

decisions.summary: Makefile FREE_TEXT and help lines for DEFER_FORM_OK, D15 restated, docs/guards.md row and rust/gate/CLAUDE.md plan row are fixed by the session before T17 lands, outside the builder's brief.
decisions.why: Fixed before the task lands, not deferred; matches the GM-approved default of fixing in the task.

decisions.why: It is improvement 4 of the six the GM ordered first on 2026-11-20 ('doing those first makes everything after them faster'), and it shortens the builders' loop, which FR-013 names.

blocks: ### T12 (FR-006: builders past a large context slowed the window's critical path - the spec's User Story 2, research R3)

decisions.summary: a new guard context_cap_hooks, PreToolUse *, after event_log_hooks in guards(); its files held by make guard-edit
decisions.why: FR-006 asks for a guard refusing a builder's tool call past a threshold; this is where and how it is placed. Nothing the request or FR-006 says is narrowed.

decisions.summary: payloads captured from Claude Code itself (claude -p, a scratch hook) rather than a dump in the clone, pinned as payloads.json
decisions.why: A method for finding the payload's real keys (agent_id, agent_type, transcript_path), labeled with date and method; it decides nothing about what is refused.

decisions.summary: no agent_id passes before any read (main session); an agent_type naming the clone's .claude/agents/<type>.md passes on a stat
decisions.why: FR-006 defines a builder as an agent with a task's brief, not a defined review agent; the main session is not an agent. Carries D8 as accepted.

decisions.summary: an agent_id that is not letters, digits, - and _ passes
decisions.why: Both the cap's measure (the transcript at subagents/agent-<agent_id>.jsonl) and its one exit (the handoff file named by the agent id) are paths built from the id; an id that cannot be joined into a path leaves neither a context to measure nor a handoff to name, so refusing would refuse with no exit. The same capture shows builders' ids are plain names, so ordinary work does not reach this path and FR-006's enforcement is not gutted.

decisions.summary: context = input + cache_read + cache_creation tokens of the last assistant row with usage above zero; user rows carrying a child's usage and zero rows skipped
decisions.why: FR-006 caps the builder's context; this measures the builder's own model call and excludes rows that are not its model calls (measured: user rows hold the child's usage). It makes the cap measure what FR-006 names.

decisions.summary: judge runs the sender's own cap first: a builder past its cap is refused its SendMessage like any other call
decisions.why: D9 refuses every tool call of a builder past the cap but the handoff write; a SendMessage is a tool call. Applies the accepted rule, narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: a target whose meta agentType is a defined agent passes
decisions.why: FR-006 defines a builder as an agent dispatched with a task's brief, not a defined review agent; D9 says a defined agent is never read.

decisions.summary: a SendMessage whose target has no agent-<to>.meta.json beside the session transcript passes
decisions.why: Without the meta file the guard cannot tell a builder from a defined review agent (agentType lives only there) and has no dispatch id; refusing there would refuse defined agents, which FR-006 excludes from the rule by definition. Telling the two apart is impossible in this case, which is more than awkward. The block measured (2026-11-20) that the session's dispatched agents carry the file, so the pass does not reach the ordinary builder. The past-cap and landed refusals both fire wherever the meta exists.

decisions.summary: the target's task is found by the brief's T<n>, then its FIRST event line's task, then the task-start entry in force at its dispatch - not D2's last rung, the latest task-start
decisions.why: D10 refuses a builder whose task has landed since it was dispatched; the task in force at dispatch is that builder's task, while the latest start may be another task's. It is a more faithful reading of 'its task' and is tested with a later open task-start in the log. It refuses more often, not less.

decisions.summary: dispatch time = the Agent PreToolUse line whose id is the meta's toolUseId, else the builder's first line, else its transcript's first timestamp
decisions.why: This is how D10's 'since it was dispatched' gets measured. Each fallback is an earlier-or-equal instant, so no landing that FR-006 counts is missed. The facts it rests on are dated and measured.

decisions.summary: landed = an end line with landed true naming the task after the dispatch (a background make land included), or the task ticked in tasks.md/tasks-done.md; a refused landing (landed false) does not count
decisions.why: FR-006 says 'whose task has landed'. A refused landing has not landed. Counting a tick with no time bound is broader than the rule, never narrower.

decisions.summary: a target under the cap with no task found anywhere passes and writes a resume-no-task record; past the cap it is still refused
decisions.why: The landed rule has no subject when no task can be found: the brief names no T<n>, the agent's first line carries none, and no task-start was in force at its dispatch. FR-006's builder is 'an agent dispatched with a task's brief', and an agent with no recoverable task cannot be told apart from a helper that has none. Refusing there would refuse non-builders, so fail-closed is not possible without contradicting FR-006's definition. The cap still applies in that case (tested: past the cap with no task, refused), and every pass is logged as resume-no-task, so the gap is measured rather than silent. It does not gut the purpose, which is one task per builder, enforced wherever a task exists.

decisions.summary: CONTEXT_OK in the SendMessage's summary passes and is recorded
decisions.why: It is D10's escape verbatim, and FR-012 requires an escape that is recorded.

A failure only in the with-line run keeps the line withdrawn and refuses (exit 2), naming it. Otherwise the line is restored and the red is reported as already there.
decisions.why: This is FR-011 (withdraw and refuse, naming the failure, on a failure the new line introduces). The masking cannot hide a new failure: an identical message at a shifted line is still counted twice in the multiset, and only line/column digits are masked, so ids such as FR-023 and FR-024 stay distinct. The pre-existing case keeps the line, as FR-011 limits refusal to failures the new line introduces.

decisions.summary: On a failed build the launcher keeps cargo's report and adds each file cargo points at (from the tree root), an advice line (yours: fix it; not yours: leave it and re-run once it compiles) and the git status of uncommitted edits; a failure naming no file keeps the old line; it applies to any uncompiling source.
decisions.why: Serves FR-013's 'the builders' loop faster': it removes the old order to edit the neighbor's file. It does not change who is refused or when, so it adds no behavior beyond the message. Its red-first shard case (2 FAIL lines on the unfixed launcher) only checks that the message is there, so it enforces the task and is not added scope.

decisions.summary: Do not build a fallback that runs the last good l7r-gate binary when the tree does not compile; the launcher stays fail-closed.
decisions.why: Neither the request nor the spec asks for a fallback. The GM's words call only for performance work to go first, and FR-013 defines it by tag. Not building one keeps existing behavior the plan must keep (feature 449 T061's fail-closed launcher, and the dispatch's rule that a gate check over a changed guard uses the new code), so it narrows nothing asked. If you read it against the task's own problem statement (others' commands blocked), it is still not a narrowing of the GM's request. On the merits it would be LEGITIMATE anyway: a fallback would let verdicts and push-trusted records come from a binary older than the code it judges, which defeats what the gate is for. The plan measured how much a fallback would cover: the commands that may run safely on an old binary were 787 of 12,700 make targets in a week (6%), and make decide (449 runs) and rust-test (2,414 runs) would still fail.

decisions.summary: Rule: a command may run on a binary older than the tree only if it renders no verdict and writes no record a later gate or push trusts. Under it decide, task-start, every check, rust lint/test/cover/dead, format --check, speckit-todo's push routes, mode-a and hamlet fail; format writing, bare speckit-todo and coord lines pass.
decisions.why: It is the reason for not building the fallback, not an exception put into behavior: nothing in the plan runs an old binary under it. It is narrower than (and so consistent with) the fail-closed launcher. The plan's figures carry one-shot measured labels (2026-11-20, .git/tool-usage.jsonl kind:target, 2026-11-13 to 20), and the arithmetic holds (787/12,700 = 6.2%).

decisions.summary: A run is the outermost make above the process; checks one make runs side by side (static beside counters-inert in make done), and runs nested in a run's tests, share it and do not wait on each other; with no make above, the process is its own run
decisions.why: This is the plan's one 'except when': runs under one outermost make share the lock. It narrows nothing in request.md. The why rests on what was measured. The make done shape (rust cover beside rust test-counters under one parent named make) joined one run, had 0 waits and both exited 0. In 12 of 12 real-cargo pairs with separate parents, the second run waited. The 5-overlaps red shows that two takers sharing one run id get no protection. The bundle has no measurement of two builders' make runs getting distinct run ids under the real harness. Not blocking: that premise is the obvious one (each builder's Bash call starts its own make), but it is unmeasured here.

decisions.summary: A member is a pid plus start time, gone when the process is; a killed run leaves nothing to clear
decisions.why: This is how the lock is implemented. A stale holder cannot wedge later runs, and no manual clearing step is needed.

decisions.summary: A second run waits, printing a line on stderr at once and every 30 s (GUESS) that names the holder (pid, check, run's make line and pid, since when) and the seconds waited

decisions.summary: Past L7R_RUST_LOCK_CEILING (default 1800 s, GUESS) the check refuses, naming the holder and 'kill <run pid>'

FR-012's first line lists only the refusals of FR-006 to FR-009 and FR-011, so it does not require a red-first test here. The block names a red-first test only for taking turns. For the refusal it claims only that the crate is at 100% of its lines, which shows the path ran, not that a test proves the refusal fires. The block calls the lock-off switch used for the cost measurement 'temporary', and item 10's list of new knobs does not include it; that list is the only evidence it does not ship. Two conditions stand, neither blocking the class: no off-switch ships, and a test shows the ceiling refusal fires.
