decisions.why: A kept result ran nothing, and `dead` reads source text with no cargo, so there are no build, test or cover seconds to book.

decisions.summary: `hamlet` writes no phase line.
decisions.why: It is a stage run of the work budget, not a check's build, test or cover, which are the kinds FR-003 names. Its Bash call is still booked whole under its make target by FR-001/FR-005.

decisions.summary: `test-times` writes no phase line.
decisions.why: It is a timing tool whose repeated runs are its own report, not the checks' phases. Its call is booked whole under its target by FR-001/FR-005.

decisions.summary: cover-build writes one line per family's group (crates named), and a failed group's crates asked again one at a time each write their own.
decisions.why: This carries D4's own per-family reading, which D4 names for the plan review, and it is not a decision of this section. A coverage build serves the whole family at once, so it cannot be timed per crate.

decisions.summary: Lines are written at kept.rs binary_key (build), side.rs run_built (test), cover.rs build (cover-build) and run_one (cover-run, none for a failed build), and lint and format per crate in answer's loop, never inside check.
decisions.why: These are D4's sites and kinds, and nothing is counted twice.

decisions.summary: The Phase row carries src, step, crates, t0, t1 and code, plus make (the outermost make's first target via shared::make::invoked, or rust-<cmd>) and clone.
decisions.why: D4 names the make target and the clone, and D1 the rust-<cmd> reading.

decisions.summary: glyph first_event and checkpoint events skip Phase/BgEnd lines through a list in reviews; stepback_bundle sessions_of and tool_yield tally_events skip them by measure's ASIDE (tally_events pinned); flow_sections, read::reversals and speckit_todo active are read and left alone.
decisions.why: This keeps the existing readers from mis-booking the new lines. It is part of making FR-003's lines work, and it adds no behavior.

decisions.summary: Fixture red-first cases for each kind (fresh and counting-free runs: build before test; no-binary: one build line) and each reader; done is measured by a real make rust-test writing its phases; ordered after T04.
decisions.why: These are verification and sequencing of the requested lines.

decisions.summary: T06 (data half, FR-003, 'Performance work? no') runs ahead of the refusals after the GM's 2026-11-20 reorder; it comes before T10, T13 and T14, which read its end line
decisions.why: The GM's 2026-11-20 words put the six improvements first. D10 and D11 (two of those improvements) read a landing from this end line, so T06 is a prerequisite of the improvement fixes. Doing it first serves the order.

decisions.summary: A new land/phase.rs writes each step's line through append_row_for in T05's row form (ev Phase, src land, step, t0, t1, t, code, make, clone). land.rs wraps each step and long_runs.rs the cohort
decisions.why: This is FR-003's 'make land its phases' seconds ... as event lines' and D5's Phase lines, written through the one writer.

decisions.summary: The steps tile the landing: cheap, gate (the whole second pass, wider than D5's '(make done)'), claims, push (the ticks, their commit, the push, a failed push's revert), and the push's tail booked to after-push
decisions.why: FR-003 names the cheap refusals, the gate, the claims round and the push. Booking every part of the landing to one of them serves the request's 'where our time went'. A wider gate books more of the landing's real time and drops nothing.

decisions.summary: cohort has its own line, nested inside the gate line's span; its code is minus the signal when a red gate stops it
decisions.why: D5 lists cohort as a step. Nesting it keeps the time from being counted twice, and its own seconds are still on its own line.

decisions.summary: cheap and claims write code 2 when they refuse; a raising step writes code 1; a step that did not run writes no line
decisions.why: These are D5's exit codes made concrete for each step.

decisions.summary: For a landing whose push went out, end is written the moment the push goes out (exit 0 or 3): landed true, and its code is the push's. It is no longer the last line, and a tail that raises leaves end at the push's code while the process exits 1. A landing that never pushed writes its end at its exit with landed false
decisions.why: D5's wording is 'a last end line with its exit code'. D5 says what that line is FOR: refusals counted from the landing's own line, and D10 and D11 reading whether a task landed. D7 reads landed 'whatever its code', so a pushed landing whose tail raised is a landing, and the tail's exit 1 still stands on the after-push line. No reader loses a fact. A refused landing still ends with its own code and landed false. This is the mechanism the previous round asked for, and it makes a stop in the tail read as landed. It departs from D5's wording, not from its outcome.

decisions.summary: A new step, after-push, books the push's tail (the fresh block's start, the work-budget view after an engine landing). It comes after end, and a raise there is its own line's code
decisions.why: FR-003 names 'the push' as a phase, and this is the push's tail, split out so that end can be written at the push. Every second is still booked to a named line. A new step name for part of a requested phase only makes the requested breakdown finer.

decisions.summary: end carries tasks split as main splits them (D16's commas, T18's) and landed
decisions.why: D5 requires tasks split as D16 splits them. D7 and D11 define landed on the end line.

decisions.summary: Each phase line carries the first task landed as task; end carries every id asked
decisions.why: A run of several tasks cannot be divided between them. D5 puts the full list on end, which is where D7, D10 and D11 read a landing, and every second is still booked.

decisions.summary: main's own refusals (no NOTE=, no feature directory) write an end for the tasks they name; a usage refusal that names no task writes none
decisions.why: D5 defines end by 'the task ids it was asked to land'. A usage refusal was asked to land nothing, so D5 owes no line for it.

decisions.summary: landed is true when the push went out (exit 0, or 3 MERGED). D7's rework, D10's and D11's landing, T13, T14 and the data model's Landing read landed, restated with this task
decisions.why: D7 and D11 in the accepted spec say exactly this. The restatement brings the other tasks into line with the spec and does not widen it.

decisions.summary: append_row_for(root, feature, row) beside append_row in the held writer (make guard-edit) files a line in the feature its word names, before T26's chain. A blank word or one naming no feature leaves the chain as it was, and T05's callers are unchanged
decisions.why: FR-005's readers read per feature. Without this, a landing of a task never started in the clone would be filed under fallback, where T13 and T14 would not find its end. It reaches only the new callers and adds no behavior beyond what the requested lines need.

decisions.summary: make is the outermost make's first goal, read from /proc as T05's lines read theirs; land when no make is above
decisions.why: This is T05's row form applied to this source.

decisions.summary: A landing stopped (make land-stop, TERM) before its push went out writes no line past its last finished step and reads as open, never as refused
decisions.why: A stop is not a refusal, and a landing stopped before its push did not land. Reading it as open answers D7, D10 and D11 correctly. The running step's split is lost, but FR-002 still books the run's span.

decisions.summary: A landing stopped in the push's tail (after-push) already has its end written, landed true
decisions.why: This closes the previous round's NOT LEGITIMATE finding. The end at the push now carries landed true before the tail starts, so D10 and D11 read the task as landed, and red-first cases cover a tail that raises after the push.

decisions.summary: One window stays open. A stop while sync-with-main.sh done runs, after the remote took the push but before the script reports it, writes no end. The section points to the push's tick commit on main as the record
decisions.why: Last round's exception rested on implementation awkwardness ('no signal handler's work'). This one rests on knowledge: until the push command reports, the landing process does not hold the fact that the remote took the push, so no writer in the landing can record landed true in that interval. A pre-push guess would write a false landed whenever the push then fails. The rule is impossible here, not merely awkward, and the section has already shrunk the gap to that interval. The tick commit on main is not what makes this legitimate: D10 and D11 as cited read the end line, not main. The real outcome in the window is that the landing reads as open, never as refused. D7's rework count therefore stays right, D10 misses a resume of that task's builder, and D11 keeps that task's static count unreset. That is one rare interleaving (a manual stop during the push itself), with the outcome confined to that one task. This is the one case the previous round's requirement ('once a landing's push has gone out, a later stop must not leave it reading as unlanded') cannot reach. The ruling covers only the interval before the script reports the push went out. The block also says 'before the script exits'. If sync-with-main.sh reports success and then goes on working before it exits, that stretch is not unknowable: end must be written when the report comes, and an end held until the exit would be outside this ruling.

decisions.summary: T18 carries only D16's first half (land.rs splits T= on commas and whitespace); task-add's quick check is left to another task
decisions.why: Splitting FR-011 between tasks narrows nothing about the feature. The request's improvement 6 ('Accept commas in T=') is carried whole here. The task-add half is not in this bundle, so whether it is planned elsewhere is for that task's own review.

decisions.summary: The change goes in rust/gate/crates/land/src/land.rs and make land's help text
decisions.why: Where the T= parser lives, plus documenting the accepted form. Both serve 'Accept commas in T='.

decisions.summary: Red-first tests: T="T1,T2" and T="T1, T2" each land both tasks in the land tests' fake world
decisions.why: D16 splits on commas and whitespace, so both forms are what FR-011 asks for. A test that fails only when commas are not accepted is enforcement of the request ('real enforcement'), not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: Ordered after T17
decisions.why: Sequencing among the approved improvement fixes, which the GM put first on 2026-11-20. Nothing is deferred behind non-improvement work.

decisions.summary: Item 12 counts a comma list refused as one unknown task as a defect (valid input refused); found-and-left none; no map, no pool manifests
decisions.why: Matches the request's framing of the comma refusal as something to fix. Nothing is left unfixed.

decisions.summary: 'Performance work? no'
decisions.why: The label leaves nothing out and changes nothing in FR-011. The task is still placed among the six improvements the GM put first (order after T17). See the note on SC-006 in the reply.

decisions.summary: The guard's consulted::context gains context_from(root, var) with the environment handed in; context delegates to it with the guard's own var, so other callers are unchanged.
decisions.why: An implementation choice for repairing a test that read the real environment (make static red on the bundle crate's coverage with SPECIFY_FEATURE exported). It changes no behavior the request or spec settles; the existing entry point keeps its behavior.

decisions.summary: The bundle crate's source_pages asks context_from with the process environment in the binary and, under cfg(test), its own thread-local map (helpers::VARS), empty unless a test names a variable.
decisions.why: Test-only seam so the test, not the builder's shell, decides the branch; the binary still reads the process environment. Nothing in request.md or the spec is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The test at helpers/tests.rs asserts the one outcome it means (code 1 and the exact AttributeError on a [1] pointer), then names SPECIFY_FEATURE in its own map and asserts the pointer skipped (code 0); red first with SPECIFY_FEATURE exported.
decisions.why: Makes the test assert exactly rather than depend on the environment; tightens a check, narrows nothing asked. Red-first runs carry dated methods.

decisions.summary: Constraint: no process-environment mutation in a test (it races other tests on the thread pool); 100% line coverage of each crate by its own tests kept.
decisions.why: A constraint on how the fix is made, not a reduction of any requested outcome.

decisions.summary: Lands before T08 (T03's plan review); independent of the land crate's work.
decisions.why: Ordering of a blocker repair (make static red stops landings); the spec does not settle T24's position and nothing requested is deferred by it.

decisions.summary: The sweep's other either-outcome tests (arbiter/tests.rs:579, gate/src/lib.rs:309, record/tests.rs:301, measure/spec/tests.rs:54, owed/.../answer_modes.rs:149) and modal.rs:866's raw CHECK_ORDER_OK read are named in the report, outside T24's edit scope, not filed.
decisions.why: Neither request.md nor the spec asks for these tests to be changed, and the plan states, with a measured probe for CHECK_ORDER_OK (78 of 78 exported, 2026-11-20), that none reads SPECIFY_FEATURE or flips with this task's defect. No wrong outcome is shown for them here, so leaving them is not a defect deferred and needs no ruling.

decisions.summary: make set-down removes the clone's active-task mark once the set-down row is written, when the mark names the set-down feature, and says so in its reply; the next task-start writes it again
decisions.why: Fixes a defect in the sense of constitution XIV (a tool refusing valid work: a set-down feature's stale mark held every push touching its specs and refused T06's landing). It removes friction from the landings this feature exists to speed up (request 2026-11-20: prioritize the improvement fixes and performance work), and it matches FR-013's own reading that a set-down feature holds no started task. It narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: A refused set-down, another feature's mark, or a mark that cannot be read or names no feature is left as it stands and fails nothing
decisions.why: None of these cases is the defect. Clearing another feature's mark, or clearing the mark after a refused set-down, would be wrong. Leaving an unreadable mark as it is does not take back any part of the stated goal: a set-down feature no longer holds pushes through its own mark.

decisions.summary: Tagged [perf] in FR-013's sense (it makes the landings faster), not filed with PERF=1 because it touches no engine stage's counted operations or time
decisions.why: FR-013 defines performance work to include a task that makes the landings faster. A stale mark cost a refused landing and reverted ticks. The PERF=1 distinction follows FR-013's two routes as written.

decisions.summary: Red-first test, 100% line coverage of the task crate, the clear deleted to show the test turns red, a scratch-repo replay of the incident, and the usual green exits
decisions.why: Verification that the fix does what it says. It is not new behavior.

decisions.summary: One reader performance(id, title, plan): the [perf] tag among the bracketed tags right after a task's id (not a quoted [perf] in prose), or PERF=1's '### T<n> Performance checklist' heading.
decisions.why: FR-013 defines performance work as a task filed with PERF=1 or tagged [perf] on its line; the reader recognizes exactly those two marks.

decisions.summary: The Stop hook's active test comes out of verdict() as active() (open box but the GM's, not set down since the last task-start, not closed by status) and is shared by task-start.
decisions.why: FR-013 defines an active feature as exactly the Stop hook's own test in set_down_hooks.rs; sharing one function is how that definition is honored.

decisions.summary: next_performance(root, git dir, prefer) picks the open performance task: the feature being started first (counted active even if set down, since its start ends that), then each other feature started in this clone, latest start first; both the Stop hook and task-start ask this one picker.
decisions.why: FR-013: task-start refuses while an open performance task exists in any active feature, and the Stop hook names one before any other. The active set is the Stop hook's own test (which reads this clone's start log); counting the feature being started as active widens, not narrows, the refusal; one picker for both keeps the hook from naming a task the start refuses.

decisions.summary: task_start.rs perf_first reads PERF_LATER_OK first (reason of two words or more, refused short, recorded in the guard log under perf-first), then refuses a non-performance task naming the picked task and its make task-start F= T= command.
decisions.why: FR-013 (refusal naming the task and the command to start it, an escape of a reason) and FR-012 (two-word recorded escape, message naming the compliant command, red-first test with the check deleted - the reds, greens and deleted-check reds are recorded).

decisions.summary: Specs read under the clone's toplevel where resolve_feature found the feature, never L7R_GATE_TREE.
decisions.why: An implementation choice of where to read the tasks FR-013's test reads; it removes no case FR-013 covers.

decisions.summary: Tagged [perf]: 451 T12-T21, T28, T29; 444 T34, T36, T43. 444 T27 and T30 already marked by PERF=1. Left untagged, each with its reason: 451 T07-T11, T22, T24; 444 T24, T25, T28, T29, T31-T33, T35, T39, T42; 449's listed open boxes; 417 (engine deleted); every box of the 20 closed features.
decisions.why: An application of FR-013's own definition (a task that makes the engine, checks, gate, landings or builders' loop faster) to the measured list of 248 open boxes; the tasks whose stated outcome is less time are tagged, including all six improvements the GM ordered first (T12-T21), and the left ones are measurement, correctness, deletion, budget or record work, or work on a deleted engine that would speed nothing. No performance-improving task is shown left out.

decisions.summary: The plan template's 'Performance work?' question is read in FR-013's sense (yes for a [perf] task; PERF=1 is the other mark and adds the checklist); T12-T19's sections flip to yes.
decisions.why: Aligns the plan's own question with FR-013's definition; the caller reports (b) and (c) done, the latter reviewed in the plan-delta round beside this.

decisions.summary: T28 is itself [perf]-tagged, not filed with PERF=1, since the checklist measures an engine stage's operations and time and a refusal's order has neither.
decisions.why: FR-013 accepts either mark; the tag makes T28 performance work in its sense.

decisions.summary: PERF_LATER_OK added to the Makefile's FREE_TEXT and named in task-start's help; recorded once by the tool itself (as plan.rs records PLAN_REVIEW_OK), with no $(LOGESCAPE) make-side line - a stated departure from D15/D16's make-side form.
decisions.why: FR-012 asks that the escape be recorded; it is, once, in the guard log, and SC-006 reads it off the escape log. The departure is of mechanism, not of anything the GM or FR-012 required, and avoids a double record.

decisions.summary: T28 lands right after T18, with T29.
decisions.why: T28 is itself performance work and the GM's 2026-11-20 order puts the remaining improvement fixes first; placing it among them honors that order.

decisions.summary: D12 is built in no_poll_hooks with the listed red-first cases. Plain & / nohup / setsid / disown on a make or cargo job is refused, naming run_in_background. A covering wait passes, DETACH_OK escapes and is recorded, and mentions pass.
decisions.why: FR-008, D12 and FR-012 settle this. It is the GM-approved improvement 3, 'a guard refusing that pattern'.

decisions.summary: A bare wait after a loop, if or case body run in the same shell covers the jobs started inside that body. D12 literally asks for 'a command of the same list as the job's &'.
decisions.why: This is unchanged from the ruling of 2026-11-20. D12's own test is that a covering wait means the call 'does not return before the run ends, so the harness tracks it', and a bare wait 'waits for every job'. Bash runs (timed by EPOCHREALTIME, 2026-11-20) showed that a bare wait in the enclosing same-shell list waits for jobs started in for, if, while, case and { } bodies. Refusing those calls would refuse tracked, correct work, which is a defect under XIV. The purpose of the request, refusing the UNTRACKED pattern, stays whole. The block keeps the ruling's limit: compounds in another shell stay refused, and wait $! and wait %N cover only in the job's own list.

decisions.summary: A compound that runs in another shell stays refused even when a later wait follows. 6 compound-in-a-pipeline cases are pinned (for ...; done | cat; wait, { make x & } | cat; wait, ..., the sixth ( make x & ) | cat; wait), and 2 waits inside the part pass. For a bare ( ), a backgrounded loop and $( ), the block states they are refused.
decisions.why: This is D12's literal rule ('in the same shell (not in a ( ) or $( ) of its own)'), and it is the limit the previous ruling set. The block says the 6 pipeline cases were already refused before they were added. With the pipeline's subshell cut deleted, 5 of the 6 went red, and the sixth is a ( ), which is a separate shell whatever the pipeline does.

decisions.summary: wait $! and wait %N cover only in the job's own list.
decisions.why: This is D12's literal rule, the stricter reading.

decisions.summary: The shared readers' defects are fixed in T15, with T30 folded in. strip_heredocs takes a heredoc whose opener line continues past its delimiter. strip_quotes keeps a quoted string only after an interpreter's -c (flags joined: bash -lc, sh -ec, python3 -c), never after grep -c or git -c, and blanks the strings quoted inside a kept one. make::invoked reads setsid [opts] as a wrapper, reads 'make;' as a call, and reads a goal-less make as .DEFAULT_GOAL; a goal it cannot read (make $T) still names none. Each fix has a red-first test, and no_poll_hooks reads through these readers, with its own readers retired.
decisions.why: This answers the previous BLOCKED finding in the first way it offered: fix the shared readers in T15 and point the guard at them. These are defects (a check passing bad work or refusing good work). Fixing them in the task that found them is the GM-approved improvement 4 ('Briefs that default to fixing in the task') and fix-as-we-go, and it serves D1's single shared detector. It adds no behavior the request did not ask for. The gate's land and rustc callers skip a goal-less make's .DEFAULT_GOAL as they skipped its empty goal before, so they keep their behavior. make $T naming no goal is not a defect left. A goal held in a shell variable cannot be read from the command text, and the job is still refused when it is backgrounded: 'for t in a b; do make $t & done | cat; wait' is among the refused cases. 'Found and left? none' is now true.

decisions.summary: Every guard is replayed on the four frozen corpora (1,134 commands) before and after the shared fix. 3 verdicts moved, each named as a correction: no-poll refuses a setsid nohup make done & launch; no-poll brackets a pkill -f "pytest" it had missed; main-tree honors a # MAIN_TREE_OK: reason that the old misreading swallowed. main-tree-refusals-2026-09.json row 130 is relabeled from rewrote to allowed, and its split moves from 109/64 to 110/63.
decisions.why: Under fix-as-we-go, a check's verdict changing as a bug is fixed is expected and is never a regression. Each moved verdict is named and shown to be a fix of the misreading. The relabeled row was recorded under that misreading, and the suite's own rule is that an escaped command is allowed, not rewritten. Correcting the label matches the guard's intended behavior. It does not change what the guard does.

decisions.summary: In the frozen corpora, the refusals (14 on the first replay, 16 now) are all real setsid nohup make done ... & / nohup make done ... & launches, read by hand, so there are 0 false refusals.
decisions.why: FR-008 and D12 name nohup and setsid at a command position without exception.

decisions.summary: Any disown after a make or cargo job's & refuses the call whatever wait follows, disown -h included.
decisions.why: D12 settles this explicitly.

decisions.summary: Tagged [perf] and ordered first in lane B. It needs only T02's make detector, which has landed.
decisions.why: The GM, 2026-11-20: 'let's prioritize those remaining improvement fixes'. FR-013 puts performance work first, and this is one of the six approved improvements.

decisions.summary: T30 does no work of its own: the shared shell readers' fix (strip_heredocs, strip_quotes, make::invoked) was folded into T15 by T15's plan review and landed there red-first, with the corpora replayed through every guard; T30 closes when T15 ticks.
decisions.why: Nothing is narrowed or left: the defect T30 was filed for is fixed, only in a different task, because T15's plan review ruled leaving it NOT LEGITIMATE. Moving where a fix lands does not shrink what was asked; 'Found and left? none'.

decisions.summary: Done is T15 ticked with the fix; the red exit records what failed, sets the task down, and routes any cannot-be-done claim through make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: A completion condition and a standard failure route; it carves out no case and defers no defect.

decisions.summary: Kept as a [perf] task under FR-013, folded into T15.
decisions.why: Classification under FR-013's own definition (work that makes the checks/gate/builders' loop faster or correct); it narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: slow_poll (split into no_poll_hooks/pace.rs under constitution X's 1,000-line bar) is called first in the POLL_OK-escaped branch and before file_wait; a payload with agent_id passes untouched by the pace check; -c strings and backgrounded calls are judged too
decisions.why: This is D13 as written: both permitted paths, before either returns, and the main session only (no agent_id). A -c string that a shell runs is the same loop spelled another way, so reading it enforces FR-008 and adds no reach. Splitting the file is housekeeping, not a decision about scope.

decisions.summary: the pace is the longest sleep at a command position inside a loop, with the head counted, s/m/h/d units read and several numbers summed as GNU sleep reads them; a quoted string, a sleep with no loop, a sleep after done and a redirection after a sleep are not a pace
decisions.why: FR-008 refuses a 'wait loop' that checks less often than 60 s. Reading the loop's real interval the way the shell would is that rule. A sleep outside a loop and a quoted string are not a checking loop, so passing them follows FR-008's wording.

decisions.summary: replaces the earlier pass of sleep $N: a variable the command sets (N=480, export, quoted, an env prefix, several assignments) is read at the largest value it is given, and a length still unreadable ($N set nowhere, arithmetic, a substitution, infinity) is refused as endless, naming the literal sleep 60 form, with SLOW_POLL_OK as the escape
decisions.why: This no longer narrows. Every main-session wait loop now gets judged, which is FR-008's rule with no carve-out. Refusing a length the guard cannot read is enforcement of the requested rule, not new behavior. The guard cannot show that such a loop checks within 60 s. The refusal names the compliant form and offers FR-012's recorded escape. The spec already does the same for D12's unreadable 'wait $P'. Taking the largest value assigned is a conservative reading of the same rule. The GM asked for 'real enforcement and not just instructions', and this closes the gap my earlier ruling left open. The plan-blocks review overruled that ruling (LEGITIMATE), and this block follows the review.

decisions.summary: a pre-existing defect is fixed: SLEEP_RE and sleep_in_loop required a digit, so a loop whose sleep takes a variable (until curl -s x; do sleep $N; done) never reached the loop branch and passed even the busy-wait refusal, a subagent's included. The branch is now entered wherever the pace reader finds a sleep in a loop
decisions.why: Under constitution XIV this is a defect: a check that passes bad work. HEAD's guard was observed letting the loop through (rc 0, with a method recorded). It sits in the file and the reader T16 changes, and fixing defects as they are found is the standing rule. The fix does not create new behavior. It makes the existing busy-wait refusal reach a spelling that had slipped past it, and the frozen corpora show 0 of 1,134 verdicts moved. That is consistent with 'the existing no-poll cases unchanged'.

decisions.summary: the refusal names the same command with every sleep over the knob at sleep 60. SLOW_POLL_OK escapes and is recorded, and it is masked before POLL_OK is read, so it grants nothing POLL_OK grants. Thin reasons (empty, one word quoted or bare, one word after the colon) are refused and pinned
decisions.why: D13 names the compliant form and the SLOW_POLL_OK escape. FR-012 requires an escape with a reason of two words or more, recorded, and a message naming the compliant command. Pinning the refusal of one-word reasons enforces FR-012's exact wording. The masking makes the escape do only what it says.

decisions.summary: the guard's own rewrites and offers, fed back from the main session, are never refused for their pace
decisions.why: Those forms are at or under the knob, so FR-008 does not reach them. Testing that they pass enforces the compliant side of the rule.

decisions.summary: a defect that predates T16 is fixed: shared::wait's condition grammar did not read proof_of_life's clause, so the guard refused its own invited file-wait rerun as a busy-wait. One existing test's expectation is changed to ask that the fed-back wait get no answer
decisions.why: The guard was refusing correct work on one of D13's two permitted paths, the path T16 adds its check to. That is a defect under XIV and is fixed as the work goes. The changed test is where the defect was hidden ('rewritten()' read a refusal as no rewrite), so changing it does not depart from 'the existing no-poll cases unchanged'.

decisions.summary: POLL_CHECK_S = 60 s, labeled GUESS at its point of change
decisions.why: FR-008 and D13 name the knob as 60 s and GUESS, and D14 asks for the label at the point of change.

decisions.summary: POLL_CHECK_S's row in D14's knob table in docs/guards.md is left to T22, which writes that table and is the close
decisions.why: This is ordering, not a narrowing. The table is still delivered inside the feature, before it closes, by the task that writes it. It is not a deferred defect, so FR-009 does not reach it. That T22 writes the table rests on the block's word, which this bundle cannot confirm.

decisions.summary: T16 is tagged [perf] under FR-013
decisions.why: T16 is improvement 3 of the six the GM approved ('a shorter poll loop on my side', 18 min). The GM ruled on 2026-11-20 that those fixes come first because 'doing those first makes everything after them faster'. Under FR-013 it makes the builders' loop faster.

decisions.summary: A make static call another guard refused (a PreToolUse line and no result line) is not counted as a run.
decisions.why: FR-007 refuses a third `make static`; a call refused before it ran is not a run on the plain reading. D11 as now quoted in spec-cited.md carries this definition (a run is a call that RAN, T14 2026-11-20), and it matches the request's improvement 2 rather than narrowing it.

decisions.summary: A make static still in flight (no PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure line yet), e.g. a foreground run in another session of the same task, is not yet counted.
decisions.why: Unchanged from the earlier ruling, on purpose: improvement 2 targets make static as the edit loop, and each iteration of a loop waits for the previous run's result, so every run feeding a loop has its result line and is counted; the gap admits only a run concurrent with another in the same task, counted the moment it finishes. The edit-loop pattern cannot live in the gap, so the request's purpose survives.

decisions.summary: The event log writer adds `makes` (every target of a multi-target call) and the count reads `make` or `makes`, so `make rust-test CRATE=x && make static` is counted.
decisions.why: Enforcement of FR-007 (and now in D11's text): without it a compound call escapes the count while the trigger fires on it. Delete FR-007 and the field has nothing to do.

decisions.summary: Count keyed on (feature, task) via filed_at's chain, reading only that feature's log; main session and builders share one count.
decisions.why: FR-007 counts per task; D11: every session and agent's run counts.

decisions.summary: Since the task's last landing with landed true naming it in `tasks` (any exit code), else its FIRST task-starts entry (second stamp compared as .000Z), else every line.
decisions.why: FR-007 'since its last landing'; D11/D10's definition (landed true resets, a refused landing does not; a later task-start resets nothing). Reading `tasks` makes a batch landing reset each of its tasks.

decisions.summary: A call whose line carries no task passes, logged passed/no-task.
decisions.why: FR-007 is scoped 'in one task'; D2 files a task wherever one is known (falling back to the clone's last task-start), so a call with no task has nothing to count against. The block's citation of 'D10's precedent' is still not supported by D10 as quoted; the decision stands on FR-007 and D2.

decisions.summary: Refusal names, per crate of the delta, `make rust-test CRATE=<c>` and the gate script's lint/format/cover --crate; `make quick` when no crate changed; then make static once before land; STATIC_OK escape with a reason; each named command pinned as passing the Bash-reading guards.

The dispatch states STATIC_OK's reason goes through the shared escape reader's two-word floor (FR-012); the block's 'a bare token refused' is consistent with it, and no decision here lowers that floor.

decisions.why: D11 and D14 as written.

decisions.why: A tooling gap rather than a defect; filing it narrows nothing of the request.

decisions.summary: A found-and-left item that says it is fixed in the task (fixed here, fixed in this task, before its tick, before T<own> lands) passes without a reason, filed id and order, unless it names an id it is filed as or lands before.
decisions.why: D15's visible sentence requires every non-none item to carry reason, id and order, so this narrows D15's text. But FR-009 refuses only an item that DEFERS a defect, and an item fixed in the task defers nothing; the GM approved 'briefs that default to fixing in the task', so requiring a filed task id of an item that is fixed would contradict the request. The guard that an item naming a filed/order id is judged as a deferral keeps the pass from being used to hide one.

decisions.summary: An item that says it is not a defect (not a defect, no wrong outcome, constitution XIV) passes.
decisions.why: Narrows D15's 'any non-none item' wording, but FR-009's own words reach only an item that 'defers a defect', and constitution XIV (the GM 2026-11-19) holds that a difference with no wrong outcome is not a defect and is not to be fixed. Demanding a filed fix task for a non-defect would apply a standard the GM struck. Same id-naming guard applies.

decisions.summary: A deferral owes 'Not fixed here' plus two words of reason, filed as T<n> (or added to / folded into), lands before T<m> (lists read whole), order id not equal to filed id, each id a box of tasks.md or tasks-done.md; make decide adds that each id is an unticked box now.
decisions.why: This is FR-009's three parts (why, filed id, order) made checkable; added to / folded into still name a filed task id; the open test at make decide makes the order real enforcement as the GM asked.

decisions.summary: A class fix is detected by every/all the before writer, reader, form, file, caller, instance, copy, site or guard, or 'each of the', and then owes an observed/measured line with its method.
decisions.why: FR-009's named forms (every writer, every form, every file of a kind) are all reached and the list is a superset of them; a mechanical trigger has to be a word test, and nothing FR-009 names falls outside it.

decisions.summary: The class test reads the found-and-left items and checklist item 12 (Before any fix).
decisions.why: FR-009 asks about the section's FIX; in the plan template the fix is declared in item 12 and the found-and-left answer, so reading those is reading the fix.

decisions.summary: make plan-delta runs the timeless half (form and ids filed in tasks.md or tasks-done.md) on a changed block; a section whose deferral's task has since landed is not refused.
decisions.why: FR-009 names make decide; running the same rule on a later edit only enforces it against a decided section being changed into an unformed one (the GM: 'real enforcement and not just instructions'). Not requiring the ids to be open after landing narrows nothing FR-009 asks, which is a check at decision time.

decisions.summary: A section decided under DEFER_FORM_OK passes make plan-delta after its block changes, the escape found in the guard log; the escape excuses only deferral findings.
decisions.why: It relaxes only the plan-delta check, which is enforcement beyond FR-009's make decide; at make decide, where FR-009 places the refusal, nothing is relaxed, and the escape was recorded with its reason as FR-012 requires.

decisions.summary: The tool records DEFER_FORM_OK itself (guard log rule defer-form-ok and dev/bypass-log/) instead of D15's $(LOGESCAPE) line, and only on a run that passes (decide once decided, plan-delta only where it excused a finding); a thin reason is refused.
decisions.why: FR-012 asks for an escape of two words or more that is recorded; it is recorded, once, whenever it is used. A run that is refused or excuses nothing did not use the escape. Mechanism choice; D15's text is restated to match (found-and-left).

decisions.summary: make plan-delta reads the guard log only for a changed block with a deferral finding, once a run, parsing only files naming the rule.
decisions.why: A cost choice that changes no outcome.

decisions.summary: plan-done.md is never read by make decide or plan-delta and the tick and landing call neither, so the 28 refused archived sections are not re-judged.
decisions.why: FR-009 is a refusal at make decide of a section being decided; archived sections were decided and ticked before the rule existed and no make decide runs on them. Nothing FR-009 asks is left out.

decisions.summary: Makefile FREE_TEXT and help lines for DEFER_FORM_OK, D15 restated, docs/guards.md row and rust/gate/CLAUDE.md plan row are fixed by the session before T17 lands, outside the builder's brief.
decisions.why: Fixed before the task lands, not deferred; matches the GM-approved default of fixing in the task.

decisions.summary: T17 is tagged [perf] under FR-013.
decisions.why: It is improvement 4 of the six the GM ordered first on 2026-11-20 ('doing those first makes everything after them faster'), and it shortens the builders' loop, which FR-013 names.

decisions.summary: a new guard context_cap_hooks, PreToolUse *, after event_log_hooks in guards(); its files held by make guard-edit
decisions.why: FR-006 asks for a guard refusing a builder's tool call past a threshold; this is where and how it is placed. Nothing the request or FR-006 says is narrowed.

decisions.summary: payloads captured from Claude Code itself (claude -p, a scratch hook) rather than a dump in the clone, pinned as payloads.json
decisions.why: A method for finding the payload's real keys (agent_id, agent_type, transcript_path), labeled with date and method; it decides nothing about what is refused.

decisions.summary: no agent_id passes before any read (main session); an agent_type naming the clone's .claude/agents/<type>.md passes on a stat
decisions.why: FR-006 defines a builder as an agent with a task's brief, not a defined review agent; the main session is not an agent. Carries D8 as accepted.

decisions.summary: an agent_id that is not letters, digits, - and _ passes
decisions.why: Both the cap's measure (the transcript at subagents/agent-<agent_id>.jsonl) and its one exit (the handoff file named by the agent id) are paths built from the id; an id that cannot be joined into a path leaves neither a context to measure nor a handoff to name, so refusing would refuse with no exit. The same capture shows builders' ids are plain names, so ordinary work does not reach this path and FR-006's enforcement is not gutted.

decisions.summary: context = input + cache_read + cache_creation tokens of the last assistant row with usage above zero; user rows carrying a child's usage and zero rows skipped
decisions.why: FR-006 caps the builder's context; this measures the builder's own model call and excludes rows that are not its model calls (measured: user rows hold the child's usage). It makes the cap measure what FR-006 names.

decisions.summary: no transcript file, or no such row in the tail, passes
decisions.why: Where no context is recorded there is no figure to compare with FR-006's threshold; refusing on no evidence would refuse builders that are under it. The capture (2026-11-20) shows the transcript exists beside transcript_path for a builder, so ordinary work does not reach this path and the request's 'real enforcement' holds.

decisions.summary: the tail is read backwards in 64 KiB steps to at most 16 MiB (both GUESS; the 16 MiB now labeled with the window's largest builder transcript, 50 MB scanned whole in 0.07 s, measured 2026-11-20, research R2); a builder whose last usage row lies further back passes
decisions.why: What lies after the last assistant row is that turn's tool results; 16 MiB of them with no assistant row between is not a shape ordinary work produces, so a builder past the cap is not let through by it in practice. The bound is a labeled GUESS knob, and the figure now beside it (a whole 50 MB transcript scanned in 0.07 s) is labeled with date and method; it speaks to cost, not to how far back a last usage row can sit, so it neither strengthens nor weakens this ruling. Not measured that no real tail exceeds 16 MiB - worth a count from the event log when the knob is retuned, not a block.

decisions.summary: CONTEXT_CAP_TOKENS GUESS 300,000; at the cap passes
decisions.why: FR-006's own knob and value, labeled GUESS.

decisions.summary: past the cap every call is refused but the handoff file's Write, the refusal naming the file and the next step (write what is done and left, stop, reply with the path; the session dispatches a fresh builder)
decisions.why: FR-006 verbatim ('but for writing its handoff file, naming the file and the next step'), and the approved improvement 1 ('a fresh builder per stage, with a handoff file').

decisions.summary: an Edit of the handoff file is let through beside its Write
decisions.why: Implied by FR-006's own words: the exception is 'writing its handoff file', and an Edit of that file is writing it. Confined to the agent's own handoff, it cannot carry task work, so the cap's purpose (no builder works on past a large context) survives.

decisions.summary: a Read of the handoff file is let through beside its Write
decisions.why: Ground that holds regardless of the stated tool behavior: a Read confined to the agent's own handoff file yields only what the builder itself wrote there, so it cannot carry task work and does not gut the cap's purpose, while the stated reason (the Write tool will not overwrite an unread file) would otherwise leave a builder with an existing handoff no exit. That premise about the Write tool carries no date and method in the block; it is not what this ruling rests on.

decisions.summary: any file in <git common dir>/l7r-handoffs/ whose name ends <agent id>.md counts as the agent's handoff
decisions.why: Applying the literal one-name rule, recomputed at each call from the event log's task, could refuse the very file the refusal named if the chain's task moved between them, leaving the builder no exit - defeating FR-006's handoff. Agent ids are unique, so no builder can write another's handoff (a case the suite refuses), and every such file sits in the handoff directory, where writing cannot carry task work. Ruled as stated, 'any file there' = in that directory. On the earlier aside: the session reports is_handoff compares the canonicalized parent directory with the handoff directory, so a path such as l7r-handoffs/../x-<id>.md resolves outside it and is refused; the carve-out stays confined to that directory.

decisions.summary: the handoff is named <task>-<agent id>.md from the event log's chain (filed_at), or <agent id>.md where the line carries no task
decisions.why: Naming the file FR-006 requires; no case is excused.

decisions.summary: a call outside any clone passes
decisions.why: On what the block establishes: D8's test of who is a builder is a stat of the clone's .claude/agents/, and the handoff path is under the clone's git common dir; outside a clone there is neither a who nor an exit to name, so a refusal there could refuse defined review agents and leave a builder no handoff to write. The premise that builders' calls are made inside clones in ordinary work is not measured in the block and no suite case is listed for this path - worth a count, not a block.

decisions.summary: CONTEXT_OK="<reason>" in a Bash command, recorded as context-ok; a bare one refused
decisions.why: FR-012: an escape of a reason of two words or more, recorded.

decisions.summary: D9's make context-ok AID= WHY= per-agent permit not built in T12; filed as T13, to land before T22; CONTEXT_OK in Bash the recorded escape meanwhile
decisions.why: Judged against FR-012, not D9 (which this task restated): every refusal the cap issues today has a recorded route past it - the refusal's compliant step (the handoff, always let through) and CONTEXT_OK in a Bash call, recorded - so FR-012's escape exists and no builder is trapped. The permit was the session's design for a resumed builder (D10's resume); it is filed and ordered, not dropped. Nothing the GM asked for is left out.

decisions.summary: in the performance lane after T15 and T16, before T13
decisions.why: FR-013 and the GM 2026-11-20 ('let's prioritize those remaining improvement fixes'); T12 is improvement 1.

decisions.summary: red-first unit and suite runs, the check-deleted run red, and the handoff Write's case through the whole guard chain
decisions.why: FR-012's red-first test and D9's whole-chain case; enforcement of what was asked.

decisions.summary: docs/guards.md row and knob-table row, rust/guard/CLAUDE.md mention, D9 restated to what was built, written by the session before the tick
decisions.why: D14's knob table and keeping the spec true to the built guard; no behavior added or excused.

decisions.summary: D10 in context_cap_hooks: a SendMessage resuming a builder past the cap, or whose task has landed since its dispatch, is refused; escape CONTEXT_OK in the summary, recorded
decisions.why: FR-006 and D10 verbatim; FR-012's red-first, recorded escape; serves the approved improvement 1 ('a fresh builder per stage').

decisions.summary: The sender's own cap is judged before resume(): a builder past its cap is refused its SendMessage like any call
decisions.why: D9 already refuses every tool call of a builder past the cap but the handoff write; this only orders the two checks.

decisions.summary: A SendMessage to an id with no agent-<to>.meta.json passes, logged resume-no-meta
decisions.why: agentType lives only in the meta file and FR-006 exempts defined agents, so a target that cannot be identified as a builder is outside the requirement's reach; refusing it would reach past what was asked. The pass is logged so such cases are countable (found-and-left item 2).

decisions.summary: No task found by D2's chain: under the cap passes with a no-task record; past the cap refused
decisions.why: The landed test needs a task and cannot apply without one; the cap clause of FR-006 still applies and is kept (the cap check needs no task). The pass is recorded.

decisions.summary: The target's task: the brief's T<n>, else its first line's task (by/aid), else the task-starts entry in force at its dispatch - never the latest start
decisions.why: D2's chain read for the builder's own task; using the start in force at dispatch rather than the latest start serves FR-006's 'its task' and avoids attributing another, later task to it.

decisions.summary: Landed = an end line with landed true naming the task after the dispatch (a background land included; a refused landing does not count), or the task ticked in tasks.md/tasks-done.md
decisions.why: FR-006 says 'whose task has landed' with no time bound; D10 adds 'since it was dispatched'. A ticked task is a landed one (make land ticks). Counting a ticked task without the dispatch bound stays inside FR-006's wording and does not narrow what is refused.

decisions.summary: Dispatch time: the Agent line whose id is the meta's toolUseId, else the builder's first line, else its transcript's first timestamp
decisions.why: Mechanics for D10's 'since it was dispatched', resting on the measured facts listed.

decisions.summary: make context-ok AID= WHY= grants a permit keyed <toplevel>/context-cap:<id>, read past the cap after the handoff check, valid an hour, recorded in the guard log
decisions.why: D9 names this permit, built with T13, on the guard-edit permit's mechanism; FR-012's recorded escape of a reason. The hour is a design constant, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Found and fixed here: context-ok's grant message reworded; resume-no-meta logged
decisions.why: Both defects fixed in the task, none deferred.

decisions.summary: Ordered after T12, T03, T06; tagged [perf] under FR-013
decisions.why: Dependencies on the line's task and the land end line; FR-013 counts work making the builders' loop faster as performance work.

decisions.summary: Run every line `make -n quick` lists (all seven checks) after the filing, setting aside only the green stamp and the closing printf; no skip list of checks deemed unable to read what task-add writes.
decisions.why: The request (improvement 6) says 'run make quick after task-add' and FR-011 says task-add runs make quick's checks. Every check runs. The stamp and the printf are not checks: the stamp records a green state for the tree, and the printf prints a message. Leaving both out catches nothing less. Dropping the skip list widens what is checked rather than narrowing it.

decisions.summary: The kept lines run side by side, each by sh -c to its own end, read from the make -n listing (backslash continuations joined) so the recipe stays the one list.
decisions.why: This is how the checks are run, not which checks run. Running each line to its own end shows every failure, including one that a sequential make quick would hide behind an earlier red. That serves FR-011's 'on any failure the new line introduces'.

decisions.summary: On a red, both files are restored to their pre-filing bytes, the checks are re-run, and failures (failed (exit N) plus each non-blank line, with only line/column numbers masked) are compared as multisets. A failure only in the with-line run keeps the line withdrawn and refuses (exit 2), naming it. Otherwise the line is restored and the red is reported as already there.
decisions.why: This is FR-011 (withdraw and refuse, naming the failure, on a failure the new line introduces). The masking cannot hide a new failure: an identical message at a shifted line is still counted twice in the multiset, and only line/column digits are masked, so ids such as FR-023 and FR-024 stay distinct. The pre-existing case keeps the line, as FR-011 limits refusal to failures the new line introduces.

decisions.summary: A make -n quick that cannot list (no Makefile) refuses before anything is written.
decisions.why: Fails closed. Without a listing the requested check cannot run, so filing anyway would skip the enforcement the GM asked to be real. It adds no reach beyond FR-011.

decisions.summary: The QUICK_OK escape is read from the environment and recorded by the task-add tool itself (escaped/quick-ok in the guard log), not through the Makefile's $(LOGESCAPE), following T28's PERF_LATER_OK precedent. The Makefile's FREE_TEXT entry and help line are done by the lead.
decisions.why: FR-012 asks for an escape of a reason that is recorded. It is recorded, once, and a real-tree probe confirmed the row (escaped/quick-ok). The choice changes where the recording happens, not what is enforced or what can be escaped, so it does not narrow the request or the spec.

decisions.summary: The escape reason must be two words and eight characters, else refused blocked/QUICK_OK-no-reason before anything is written.
decisions.why: FR-012 asks for 'a reason of two words or more'. Requiring eight characters as well makes the escape harder to use, which does not narrow the enforcement. The GM asked that enforcement be real (2026-11-19 approval).

decisions.summary: Tests: the four red-first cases, the check-deleted run (five red), the every-line pin (the ruff line asserted run), and the guard-log isolation pin.
decisions.why: Enforcement of FR-011 and FR-012's red-first requirement. Each test only fails when the requested behavior is absent.

decisions.summary: Found and left: the two real-tree probe rows in ~/.claude/guard-log and the rust/gate/CLAUDE.md task row not naming task_add/quick.rs are judged not defects.
decisions.why: Neither is a wrong outcome. The log rows are the measurement's own records, in an untracked log. The index line misdirects no tool and blocks no work. The QUICK_OK help/FREE_TEXT gap is fixed in this task, not deferred.

decisions.summary: T20 builds the shard form only, proved on test-parts.sh (split 6 + 7 cases plus 16 new pins); the three slow suites' splits, entry-gate.sh included, are T21's, landing before T22
decisions.why: D17 settles exactly this split of work: 'T20 builds the form, proved on test-parts.sh; T21 splits the three'. The found-and-left entry-gate deferral is that same assignment, not a defect left; every case of test-parts.sh still runs (13 before, 6 + 23 after).

decisions.summary: A shard is tests/hooks/test-<name>.<k>.sh with k all digits, run in numeric order with gaps allowed; each shard is its own job <guard>.<k> with its own .rc/.log/.s/.reads and stamps nothing
decisions.why: D17's 'tests/hooks/test-<name>.<k>.sh ... treats each shard as a job keyed by the suite's stamp key'; the per-shard .s is the measure D17 and SC-004 name.

decisions.summary: hookrun.sh --close stamps the suite (sha, trace from every shard's reads, shard list .jobs) only when every shard's job is ok; one red or missing shard leaves it unstamped
decisions.why: D17: 'stamps the suite green when every shard is'. One stamp per suite is the mechanism that delivers that without losing shards' reads.

decisions.summary: Recipe keys each shard as its own name via deps --keys and hashes the guard's key with its shards' keys; an edited or added shard reruns the suite; no change to rust/guard
decisions.why: Implementation of D17's 'keyed by the suite's stamp key'; it keeps the skip-when-unchanged behavior correct for shards and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: GUARD WITHOUT A TEST accepts a guard's suite or its shards (one hookrun.sh --jobs call); a suite beside its own shards fails as SUITE AND SHARDS BOTH; an orphan shard fails as SHARD WITHOUT ITS SUITE; a single-shard guard is accepted
decisions.why: D17: 'its companion check accepts shards for a guard's companion' and shards sit 'beside nothing else of that name'. The two refusals only fail when D17's form is broken, so they enforce what was asked.

decisions.summary: test-land-tooling.sh case 2b's wall-clock overlap bound (.checks < 1.8) is replaced by a barrier: each job marks its start and waits up to 20 s for the other's mark, and the case asserts both saw the other; timings stay recorded as numbers
decisions.why: A check that refused correct work under load (3 of 3 failed at load, recorded) is a defect, and fixing it is owed under fix-as-we-go. It still enforces the same property, that the two jobs overlap: run one after the other it went red 2 of 2. It narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: T20 expects no wall saving (parts.sh was never on the critical path); the saving is T21's; before/after equal within noise
decisions.why: It follows from D17's T20/T21 division; FR-010's 20 s bar is met by T21's splits, and SHARD_BAR_S is never a gate per D17.

decisions.summary: One environment reader for the guard crate, shared::env (opt, var; test-build set, unset): the process variable outside cfg(test), a per-test-thread map under it; consulted::var and VARS become re-exports of it (T24's seam, one map); arbiter/tests.rs pins the seam.
decisions.why: Implementation design of the fix T32 exists for. The defect is a wrong outcome: guard tests go red because a page session's shell exports a variable. A builder no longer losing rounds to that red serves the GM's 2026-11-20 request to put performance improvements first (FR-013: the builders' loop). Nothing the GM asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Fix the 6 tests that the 79-variable sweep showed moving (RECORD_CHECKS_DIR, L7R_GUARD_TREE, SET_DOWN_ROOT, L7R_PERMIT_NOW x2, L7R_DISPATCHER), and stop the event-log tests writing fixture logs into an exported L7R_EVENTS_DIR.
decisions.why: Known defects of the same kind, fixed in the task that found them (fix as we go). The stray event-log writes matter directly to this feature, because they corrupt the logs that where-time and the GM's retrospective read.

decisions.summary: Convert the 7 tests that set the process environment to set the test thread's own map, converting their reads with them.
decisions.why: Same mechanism, same task. It widens no behavior beyond the guard crate's tests.

decisions.summary: Leave log::quiet's GUARD_LOG_DIR set once for the whole process (T009), and leave the binary's main.rs and bench.rs reading the real environment.
decisions.why: Neither is a wrong outcome. GUARD_LOG_DIR is set once on purpose, to keep test logs out of real ones. main.rs and bench.rs are not tests and must read the real environment. The GM's request asks for no rule against process-environment mutation; that wording is the task line's own. Leaving a difference that works is not a narrowing (constitution XIV).

decisions.summary: Leave MEASURE_STATE_DIR (a test created the directory empty and wrote nothing into it) and the reads that the sweep showed moving no test, as not defects.
decisions.why: Measured to produce no wrong outcome (ls of the exported directory; per-var.tsv). Under constitution XIV these are not defects, and nothing the GM asked is left undone.

decisions.summary: The gate crates' tests reading the real environment through the guard (49 tests in 7 crates red with L7R_FEATURE_DIRECTORY and L7R_EVENTS_DIR exported) are not fixed in T32. decisions.summary: test-sync-with-main.sh is left whole (its split was built, measured and reverted); its full-run 26.8-40.2 s past the 20 s bar is now stated in found-and-left

The block's measurements show the split defeats that purpose: full runs equal HEAD (mean 44.0 vs 43.9 s), the incremental run after a sync-with-main edit is slower with it split (12.7/12.1 s all-three vs 11.8/11.8 s l7r-gate alone), and its shards (8.7 + 7.7 + 4.0 s) cost more than the 5.0-7.7 s whole. It does not set the wall: re-read from the named logs /tmp/t21m/r1-4 and rm1-4-head-j8-c22.log, entry-gate finishes 10.1-14.8 s after it in every one of those eight runs, and its range 26.8-40.2 s matches them (40.2 is rm1, a run whose entry-gate took 51.5 s and which the entry-gate list drops as overlapped; without it 26.8-31.0 s - the stated range is the wider, not a hidden one). The earlier gap (SC-004's letter missed by a second suite, undisclosed) is closed: it is disclosed with figures and reasoning. Leaving a GUESS bar (D17) unmet with no wrong outcome is not a defect left (constitution XIV), so this is not deferral of a defect.

The ruling rests on the chain being pursued as its own task so the request's purpose (entry-gate no longer setting the floor) is not dropped; the dispatch states it is filed as T40, an open [perf] box, which under FR-013 / SC-006 goes first. The 20 s bar is a GUESS, never a gate (D17); the request names no figure.

decisions.summary: T39 stays a [perf] task under FR-013 and closes with no change.

decisions.summary: T37 is filed as a [perf] task under FR-013.

decisions.summary: The heading-carry defect found while doing the work is fixed here, pinned by a red-first test.

decisions.summary: The one-file path feeds the file to the toolchain's rustfmt on standard input, run from the file's directory (so rustfmt.toml is found), with --edition taken from the owning crate's Cargo.toml (2015 where it names none), and writes the file only where rustfmt passed and changed it.

Standard input was chosen on a dated scratch measurement showing that a path argument rewrites the file's `mod` children, which would break 'formats only what it names'. The plan's step 9 records that `--check --crate` was clean after FILE= runs, so the output matches cargo fmt.

decisions.summary: A Cargo.toml edition that is not a literal (for example an inherited one) is refused on the FILE= path.
decisions.why: This refuses an input it cannot read rather than guessing an edition and formatting wrongly. CRATE= and bare `make format` still cover such a crate. It does not narrow anything the request or spec asks for.

decisions.summary: FILE=/CRATE= format takes no run lock and never waits on another run's tests, because it builds nothing.
decisions.why: This serves the performance purpose (FR-013, the builders' loop) and does not narrow any requirement.

decisions.summary: FILE= given together with CRATE= is refused (exit 2), and the `format` failure's tip names CRATE= and FILE= instead of bare `make format`.
decisions.why: Usage guarding, and pointing builders at the scoped forms, serve the task's own purpose (not rewriting another builder's in-progress files). Nothing is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Found and left (a): the make-only guard does not refuse a bare `rustfmt`. Deferred to T33 (held writes through a route the guard does not read), which lands before T22.
decisions.why: This is a narrowing because the block calls it a defect (a check that lets bad work through), and approved improvement 4 makes fixing in the task the default for briefs. FR-009, judged against its index line only since the bundle carries nothing more, requires a deferral to state why the defect is not fixed here, and this one does. The guard is rust/guard, where T31's builder has work in progress. Fixing it inside T34 means editing, linting and covering a crate that holds another builder's half-done files, which is the clobbering of in-progress work that T34 exists to stop, and T34's green exit cannot be met honestly over that crate now. So a literal fix-in-task would defeat the task's purpose. The defect is not left: it is filed in this feature as T33, with an order (before T22), and T33's class (writes by a route the guard does not read) matches it exactly.

decisions.summary: Found and left (b): the make-only guard's block message advertises bare `make format`, which rewrites every crate. Deferred with (a), 'Filed as T33'.
decisions.why: Ruled separately from (a), because a message's wording is not a 'route the guard does not read' and T33's class argument does not reach it. Only the location argument carries it. That argument is enough: the message text lives in rust/guard, where T31's builder works now, so the same purpose-level and exit-level reasons as (a) apply. The interim harm is reduced inside T34 itself, since `make format`'s own failure tip and `make help` now name FILE= and CRATE=. The block's 'Filed as T33' covers its whole bullet, both the guard gap and the message, so T33 owes the message fix as well as the refusal. A T33 that fixes only the refusal would leave (b) unfixed.

decisions.summary: Feature 204's D5 ('every python3 -c is a write') narrowed: a -c program a denylist of known writers judges read-only (read-mode opens only, no substitution/expansion, no relative or locally-answerable import) is marked how=read and is no write, unless the command also runs Python from stdin.
decisions.why: Not a narrowing of feature 451's request or spec (the D5/D6 in spec-cited.md are 451's own decisions; 204's D5 is known only as the plan quotes it). Ruled anyway. rulings.md is empty, so the session's own ruling carries no weight; the ground is the constitution's defect definition: a guard that refuses or rewrites a read refuses good work. D5's premise ('its cost is now zero') is measured false where no clone resolves (80 corpus rows refused clone-unresolved, 79 rewritten, replay 2026-11-20). D5's purpose (no false allow) is kept by the conservative conditions and the stdin rule (parse#72, window#61 refused as before). The denylist ends in '...', so its full reach is not visible in the bundle; not a finding.

decisions.summary: A -c read stays a write when any segment of the same command runs Python from stdin (python3 -, heredoc, < file, | python3).
decisions.why: Keeps T31 from turning measured heredoc writers (parse#72, window#61) from refused into allowed; it adds no allowance.

decisions.summary: Three real heredoc reads (main-tree#147, window#339, window#361) stay refused or rewritten, as before T31, as the stdin rule's cost; recorded under Found and left and homed in T42, which retires the stdin rule once stdin bodies are judged, landing before T22.
decisions.why: The previous round's BLOCKED asked for exactly this: the known defect now has a home. Found and left names the three rows, how they were found (the replays' rows that moved back against the stage-1 build, each hand-read), why T31 does not fix them (no stdin reader exists, and lifting the rule without one lets parse#72's and window#61's writes through - trading a refused read for an allowed write), and a filed task (T42) that retires the rule once stdin bodies are judged, ordered before T22. T31 does not worsen these rows (they were refused or rewritten before it). Limit: T42's own task line (said in the dispatch to commit to retiring the rule, red first on these three rows) is not in the bundle; the block's own words 'which retires the rule once stdin bodies are judged' are what was read.

decisions.summary: Four rows that also run a script (main-tree#103 scratch script; window#60, #62, #308 the mirror's own test suites and hooks), refused or moved before only by the -c write, now run as typed without being shown to write nothing.
decisions.why: T31 changes nothing about how a script run is judged: the same commands without the -c read are allowed today, so their earlier refusal was a side effect of the defect fixed (a read misjudged as a write). The hand-read found no writer in any of the four, unlike parse#72/window#61, so no defect is shown, and keeping a misjudged read refused to cover an unjudged segment would keep the defect. Item 1's 'every write is still moved or refused as before' slightly overstates this for these rows; item 4 discloses it.

decisions.summary: Judging Python heredoc/stdin bodies for writes (301 corpus rows main-tree allows before and after) deferred to T42, landing before T22.
decisions.why: A defect left (writes in the mirror passed), but it predates T31 and T31 does not worsen it (301 allowed before and after, measured 2026-11-20). It is outside the -c scope, needs a new reader with its own replay, is recorded under Found and left with its reason, and is homed in a filed task (T42) with an ordering (before T22).

decisions.why: FR-013 accepts either PERF=1 or a [perf] tag; each refused or rewritten read costs a builder a model round trip, builders'-loop speed in FR-013's sense.

decisions.summary: T40's goal restated from 'the full run's wall falls' to 'the suite measurably faster alone and in an incremental run that reruns it', after measurement showed the full run's wall now set by the run's total work over its 8 jobs rather than this suite.
decisions.why: What the GM asked (improvement 5, approved 2026-11-19) is a faster `make hooks-test`; FR-010 asks that the slow suites be split into shards of about 20 s, and FR-013 that performance work go first. Neither the request nor the spec names the full run's wall as the target; that was this task's own first framing. The restated goal still serves the request: the incremental run, the common case, fell 2.2-5.9 s per alternated pair with the suite still setting its wall, and the suite alone fell about 3.7 s. Dropping the full-run target cuts nothing the GM asked for. The measured reason it cannot be the target (once cut, the suite no longer sets the wall, and the cuts remove no CPU work) is a physical limit on what this task's files can reach, not a convenience.

decisions.summary: The three --answer calls in answer_all run together and are then waited on; this moves work and removes none.
decisions.why: A test-suite speed change that keeps every case and assertion. The gate's output was held identical, and the suite still goes red on a broken gate (12 passed, 1 failed with --unanswered dropped).

decisions.summary: The fixture clones with --no-checkout and makes a sparse checkout of the three paths the suite uses (8,499 of 28,472 files); case 7's find is quiet when dev/bypass-log is absent.
decisions.why: It removes checkout and index work. Both clones were driven through the eight states and the outputs diffed identical, and case 7 still counts the bypass records before and after one gate. Nothing the suite checks is dropped.

decisions.summary: Both cuts are kept although CPU-seconds did not fall (incremental 158-182 before against 171-190 after; system time down about 3 s, user time up about 12 s).
decisions.why: The request is for a faster `make hooks-test` in wall time. CPU-seconds are not part of what was asked, and the wall was measured faster in the common case and alone. A flat or slightly higher CPU cost is a cost, not a wrong outcome (constitution XIV), so keeping the cuts narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: A --depth 1 single-pack clone and a fixture shared between cases were rejected on measurement.
decisions.why: Design choices among ways to speed up the suite, with measured reasons. Nothing requested is dropped.

decisions.summary: Every owed-units computation re-reads 1,951 base blobs (0.63-1.13 s of each 1.4-1.6 s computation). The fix is deferred to T43, a change to the owed crate's Delta::fetch outside this task's files, filed to land before T22.
decisions.why: This is a performance cost, not a defect: no wrong outcome, no check's verdict changes. It is filed as its own task, not left unfiled, and ordered ahead of T22, so FR-013's performance-first order still reaches it. It also reaches every gate run, including the push, not only this suite. Putting it in a separate task with its own landing is scheduling, not a narrowing of what was asked.

decisions.summary: push-gate skip's unscoped `git diff --name-only HEAD` (0.24 s a gate run on the full clone) is judged not a defect and is not filed.
decisions.why: Under constitution XIV a defect is a wrong outcome, and a 0.24 s cost is not one. FR-013 orders performance tasks first but does not require every observed cost to be filed. A real gate pays this once a push, and the sparse clone already shrinks the index this suite walks. Nothing the GM asked for is left undone.

decisions.summary: Measure the failure in a scratch clone first, then change only the launcher's build-failure path; no gate crate changed.
decisions.why: A [perf] task under FR-013 (the builders' loop). The GM asked that performance work go first (2026-11-20) and named no mechanism for this one; confining the change to the launcher narrows nothing he or the spec asked for.

decisions.summary: On a failed build the launcher keeps cargo's report and adds each file cargo points at (from the tree root), an advice line (yours: fix it; not yours: leave it and re-run once it compiles) and the git status of uncommitted edits; a failure naming no file keeps the old line; it applies to any uncompiling source.
decisions.why: Serves FR-013's 'the builders' loop faster': it removes the old order to edit the neighbor's file. It does not change who is refused or when, so it adds no behavior beyond the message. Its red-first shard case (2 FAIL lines on the unfixed launcher) only checks that the message is there, so it enforces the task and is not added scope.

decisions.summary: Do not build a fallback that runs the last good l7r-gate binary when the tree does not compile; the launcher stays fail-closed.
decisions.why: Neither the request nor the spec asks for a fallback. The GM's words call only for performance work to go first, and FR-013 defines it by tag. Not building one keeps existing behavior the plan must keep (feature 449 T061's fail-closed launcher, and the dispatch's rule that a gate check over a changed guard uses the new code), so it narrows nothing asked. If you read it against the task's own problem statement (others' commands blocked), it is still not a narrowing of the GM's request. On the merits it would be LEGITIMATE anyway: a fallback would let verdicts and push-trusted records come from a binary older than the code it judges, which defeats what the gate is for. The plan measured how much a fallback would cover: the commands that may run safely on an old binary were 787 of 12,700 make targets in a week (6%), and make decide (449 runs) and rust-test (2,414 runs) would still fail.

decisions.summary: Rule: a command may run on a binary older than the tree only if it renders no verdict and writes no record a later gate or push trusts. Under it decide, task-start, every check, rust lint/test/cover/dead, format --check, speckit-todo's push routes, mode-a and hamlet fail; format writing, bare speckit-todo and coord lines pass.
decisions.why: It is the reason for not building the fallback, not an exception put into behavior: nothing in the plan runs an old binary under it. It is narrower than (and so consistent with) the fail-closed launcher. The plan's figures carry one-shot measured labels (2026-11-20, .git/tool-usage.jsonl kind:target, 2026-11-13 to 20), and the arithmetic holds (787/12,700 = 6.2%).

decisions.summary: L7R_GATE_STALE_OK=1 (T129) still runs the old binary, unchanged.
decisions.why: This is behavior that already exists. The plan neither widens nor removes it, and nothing the GM asked reaches it.

decisions.summary: Lands after T40 and is independent of T43. Green exit: the shard's new cases pass and the real make decide against a broken guard prints the two lines. Done is measured (exit 2 in 0.23 s with the named file and the advice).
decisions.why: Sequencing and the measures of done; they narrow nothing the request or spec asks.

decisions.summary: T43 is filed as [perf] work under FR-013 (the owed computation every gate run, push and landing pays).
decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-20: 'can we in general priotitize performance improvements going forward?' and 'doing those first makes everything after them faster'; FR-013 defines perf work as making the checks, gate or landings faster, which this is.

decisions.summary: Delta::fetch reads a base file from the working tree when the cached diff does not name it, ls-files -v does not flag it assume-unchanged/skip-worktree, it is a plain file and holds no carriage return; decoded as cat_blobs decodes, so texts equals cat_blobs.
decisions.why: A speed change that removes work; the conservative conditions keep every owed unit the same, so no check's verdict changes. Nothing the GM asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The rule applies at any revision, so --between's reads shrink too.
decisions.why: Same speed change over the same function; no behavior asked for is removed.

decisions.summary: Rejected keying the base read by merge base and reusing it across computations.
decisions.why: A design choice among speedups; it keeps an existing invariant of delta.rs and narrows nothing requested.

decisions.summary: Red-first tests on a cost counter (blobs_asked: 11 to 1) and texts-equals-cat_blobs across edited/deleted/skip-worktree/link/CR/untracked/assume-unchanged states.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the task's own hold (owed output the same, base read shrunk); a test that fails only when the requested behavior is absent serves the request.

decisions.summary: If the cached git diff or ls-files -v fails, nothing is called unchanged and every base name goes to cat-file, as before T43; tested by corrupting the index.
decisions.why: Closes a wrong outcome the new read path would otherwise introduce (edited tree read as the base, so the record family owes nothing); fixing a found defect in the step is the standing rule, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Delta::changed returns git's error on a failed diff in a repository (a corrupt index), and every owed computation reading it refuses with 'cannot tell what changed ... repair the index' rather than owing nothing (or owing everything).
decisions.why: A found defect (a check passing bad work: six modal-research units went unowed on a corrupt index, measured) fixed in the step where found, red first; the refusal is confined to the failed-diff case the defect lives in, and choosing refusal over a flood is design, not a narrowing of anything asked.

decisions.summary: The failed-diff refusal is split: where the diff fails and git rev-parse --git-dir fails too (no repository at all, asked only after a failed diff), changed is empty and nothing is owed, as before T43; a repository whose diff fails (a corrupt index) is refused. Red first (a_tree_with_no_repository_has_nothing_changed), prompted by land's replay_owing test running triage in a bare directory.
decisions.why: Keeps the pre-T43 behavior for a directory with nothing to judge (no repository, so no base and no delta) - not a wrong outcome, and the defect the refusal fixes (a corrupt index leaving six modal units unowed) is still refused, since rev-parse --git-dir succeeds on a repository whose index is corrupt. Confining a defect fix to the case the defect lives in narrows nothing the GM asked; the GM's request is performance work and this preserves existing tested behavior rather than removing any.
